creature.woolly-rhinoceros.abilities.col: The woolly rhinoceros treats environmental cold effects as if they were one step less severe.
creature.woolly-rhinoceros.abilities.rhi: The rhinoceros Strides twice, then makes a horn Strike. As long as the rhinoceros moved at least 20 feet, the Strike's damage increases to 3d12+6. A Medium or smaller creature struck by this attack must succeed at a DC 24 Reflex save or be automatically [[action.shove|Shoved]] back 5 feet and knocked [[condition.prone|prone]] by the force of the blow.
creature.woolly-rhinoceros.name: Woolly Rhinoceros
creature.wraith.abilities.grip-of-fear.t: The wraith reaches into an adjacent creature's chest, gripping their heart. The target takes 6d6 mental damage with a DC 24 basic Will save. On a critical failure, the creature is also [[condition.paralyzed|paralyzed]] until the start of the wraith's next turn.
creature.wraith.abilities.robes-of-welco: The wraith wraps its robes around an adjacent living creature, exposing it to void's embrace. If any creature is cursed by the wraith's void's embrace, the wraith can't impose void's embrace on another creature.
creature.wraith.abilities.sunlight-power: While in sunlight, a wraith is [[condition.blinded|blinded]] and [[condition.slowed|slowed 2]].
If the victim succeeds at a saving throw against this curse while in sunlight, the curse ends. While you have this curse, you bypass the resistance of the wraith that cursed you; **Saving Throw** DC 24 Will; **Stage 1** the victim is [[condition.dazzled|dazzled]] in any light (1 hour); **Stage 2** the victim gains [[ability.lifesense|lifesense]] 30 feet but is [[condition.blinded|blinded]] in any light (1 hour); **Stage 3** as stage 2, but the creature also has [[ability.void-healing|void healing]] (1 hour); **Stage 4** the victim becomes [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]] and can't awaken (1 day); **Stage 5** the creature dies and becomes a wraith, its body crumbling to ash
creature.wraith.name: Wraith
The wyvern Flies up to their fly Speed and must both move forward at least 20 feet and descend at least 10 feet. If they end the movement within melee reach of at least one enemy their size or smaller, they can make a claw Strike against that enemy. If the claw hits, as a free action, the wyvern can either automatically [[ability.grab|Grab]] the target or knock it [[condition.prone|prone]].
creature.wyvern.abilities.punishing-mome: The wyvern grabbed a creature this turn using Powerful Dive

The wyvern can [[action.fly|Fly]] at half Speed while holding the creature in their claws, carrying that creature along with them and dropping it at the end of their movement. Alternatively, the wyvern can Strike the creature with their stinger with a +2 circumstance bonus.
creature.wyvern.abilities.savage.name: Savage
creature.wyvern.abilities.savage.text: The wyvern makes a stinger Strike against the triggering creature.
creature.wyvern.abilities.savage.trigger: A creature [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]] or [[condition.restrained|restrained]] by the wyvern critically fails a skill check to [[action.escape|Escape]]
creature.wyvern.abilities.wyvern-venom.t: **Saving Throw** DC 22 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d6 poison damage (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d6 poison damage (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d6 poison damage (1 round)
creature.wyvern.name: Wyvern
creature.wyvern.strikes.claw.name: claw
creature.wyvern.strikes.fangs.name: fangs
creature.wyvern.strikes.stinger.name: stinger
creature.xoarian.abilities.body-thief.te: The xoarian squeezes itself into the head of a creature dead no longer than a day, consuming and replacing that creature's brain. At the start of the xoarian's next turn, the body revives at its maximum Hit Points, controlled by the xoarian. The xoarian is conscious and can sense everything the possessed body could. Any effect that ends the possession kills the host body with the same effects as Exit Body. The xoarian can't use any of the host creature's spells with Body Thief but can use its own innate spells.
creature.xoarian.abilities.exit-body.req: The xoarian is controlling a body with Body Thief
creature.xoarian.abilities.exit-body.tex: The xoarian bursts out of its host body, which dies instantly and is no longer a suitable host for any Body Thief ability. The xoarian stretches to its full size in an adjacent space.
creature.xoarian.abilities.ravage.name: Ravage
creature.xoarian.abilities.ravage.text: The xoarian makes two tentacle Strikes against a single [[condition.paralyzed|paralyzed]], [[condition.restrained|restrained]], or [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]] creature. If the target has 0 Hit Points after Ravage, the xoarian can use a free action with the [[trait.death|death]] trait to kill the target and occupy it with Body Thief.
creature.xoarian.abilities.stolen-identi: While a xoarian uses Body Thief, it gains the ability to understand and speak all languages known by the host, as well as knowledge of the host body's abilities, identity, role in society, and personality. However, it does not gain the specific memories or knowledge of the host body.
The xoarian senses a creature's mental essence as a precise sense with the listed range; it cannot sense [[trait.mindless|mindless]] creatures with thoughtsense.
creature.xoarian.name: Xoarian
creature.xoarian.strikes.tentacle.name: tentacle
creature.xulgath-leader.abilities.weaken: A creature hit by a xulgath leader's jaws or claw Strike is [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled 1]] (or enfeebled 2 on a critical hit) for 1 round.
creature.xulgath-leader.name: Xulgath Leader
creature.xulgath-skulker.abilities.hidde: If a xulgath skulker starts their turn [[condition.undetected|undetected]] by a creature or merely [[condition.hidden|hidden]] from it, that creature is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] against the skulker's attacks until the end of the skulker's turn.
creature.xulgath-skulker.abilities.mask-: The stalker masks their stench with curated herbs, suppressing their stench aura. The skulker can resume their stench aura as a free action.
creature.xulgath-skulker.abilities.sneak: A xulgath skulker deals an additional 1d6 precision damage to [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] creatures.
creature.xulgath-skulker.name: Xulgath Skulker
creature.xulgath-warrior.name: Xulgath Warrior
creature.yamaraj.abilities.beetle-breath:
The yamaraj breathes a blast of beetles in a 50-foot cone that deals 14d8 slashing damage and 4d8 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent slashing damage]] to creatures in the area with a DC 42 Reflex save. It can't use Beetle Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [[condition.sickened|sickened 1]].

**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is sickened 2.

**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is sickened 3.
creature.yamaraj.abilities.final-judgmen: A yamaraj's [[spell.manifestation|manifestation]] spells are used only to pronounce judgment, typically either to restore a dead or destroyed creature to life, bind a creature to the realm of the dead, or banish a creature from the realm of the dead.
creature.yamaraj.abilities.lightning-dri: Whenever a yamaraj would take electricity damage if not for its immunity, its fast healing increases to 40 on its next turn. During that turn, if it uses Beetle Breath, the beetles deal 2d12 additional electricity damage.
creature.yamaraj.abilities.shepherds-tou: A yamaraj's Strikes have the benefit of a ghost touch property rune and deal an additional 3d6 void damage to living creatures or 3d6 vitality damage to undead.
creature.yamaraj.abilities.yamaraj-venom: While a creature is [[condition.clumsy|clumsy]] from this poison, it is [[condition.doomed|doomed]] with the same value; **Saving Throw** DC 42 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 10 rounds; **Stage 1** 3d8 poison damage and [[condition.clumsy|clumsy 1]] (1 round); **Stage 2** 5d8 poison damage and clumsy 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 7d8 poison damage and clumsy 3 (1 round).
creature.yamaraj.name: Yamaraj
creature.yamaraj.strikes.claw.name: claw
creature.yamaraj.strikes.jaws.name: jaws
creature.yamaraj.strikes.tail.name: tail
creature.yeti.abilities.arctic-passage.t: The yeti ignores difficult terrain caused by ice or snow.
creature.yeti.abilities.grisly-arrival.t: Each enemy within 30 feet that witnesses the attack (including the target of the attack) must attempt a DC 23 Will save. On a failure, the creature is [[condition.frightened|frightened 2]]; on a critical failure, it's frightened 4.
The yeti hits a creature in the first round of combat and the yeti was [[condition.hidden|hidden]] from that creature at the start of combat
creature.yeti.abilities.nightmare-guardi: Yetis gain a +4 status bonus to saves against fear and against spells and abilities that affect dreams. A yeti who falls prey to a supernatural nightmare loses this ability and becomes permanently enraged, gaining a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls and a –1 status penalty to AC.
creature.yeti.abilities.rend.name: Rend
creature.yeti.abilities.snowblind.name: Snowblind
creature.yeti.abilities.snowblind.text: When [[action.hide|Hiding]], the yeti is [[condition.concealed|concealed]] by any snowfall, even if it's not thick enough to make other creatures concealed.
creature.yeti.abilities.vanish.name: Vanish
creature.yeti.abilities.vanish.text: The yeti Strides or [[action.climb|Climbs]] up to half its Speed to a location where it can Hide, then Hides. If its new [[skill.stealth|Stealth]] check result meets or exceeds the triggering creature's Perception DC, the yeti remains hidden.
creature.yeti.abilities.vanish.trigger: The yeti is [[condition.hidden|hidden]] or [[condition.undetected|undetected]] while not in combat, and a creature would observe it
creature.yeti.name: Yeti
creature.yeti.saves.note: +4 status to all saves vs. [[trait.fear|fear]] and [[trait.dream|dreams]]
creature.yeti.strikes.claw.name: claw
creature.young-adamantine-dragon.abiliti: Once the adamantine dragon is reduced to fewer than half their Hit Points, their resistance is reduced by 10 and they gain a +10 circumstance bonus to their Speeds.
The dragon's unarmed melee Strikes are adamantine.
The dragon belches a mass of boulders that deals 8d8 bludgeoning damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 28 basic Reflex save). They can't use Avalanche Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

The dragon [[action.burrow|Burrows]], then [[action.leap|Leaps]] out of the ground, landing at a point within 25 feet. The dragon makes a melee Strike against a creature within reach when they land. If the Strike is a critical hit, the target is knocked [[condition.prone|prone]].
The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Avalanche Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
The dragon's tough scales ward off deadly attacks. The dragon attempts a DC 17 flat check. On a success, the triggering attack becomes a normal hit.
The dragon is critically hit with a weapon or unarmed attack
The dragon can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 20 feet. They can leave a tunnel if they desire, and they usually don't.
creature.young-adamantine-dragon.name: Young Adamantine Dragon
creature.young-conspirator-dragon.abilit: once per day
Conjure Disguise

The dragon conjures a perfect flesh-suit replica of a [[trait.humanoid|humanoid]] they've seen of their size or smaller and compresses themself into it, along with generating appropriate clothing for the humanoid. This process takes 1 minute to complete, during which the dragon is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]]. If the dragon stops or is interrupted in this process, the suit is destroyed. Once the process is complete, the dragon can remain in this disguise indefinitely.

The transformation has the effects of [[ability.change-shape|Change Shape]], except that the disguise is not actively magical in nature and doesn't register as [[trait.magical|magical]] to [[spell.detect-magic|detect magic]] and similar effects. The dragon loses Retract Body while transformed.

If the dragon is critically hit while wearing the disguise, the suit is destroyed and immediately explodes. This has the effects of Detonate Disguise, except that creatures use the outcome one degree of success better than they rolled on their save.
Detonate Disguise
The dragon is wearing their conjured disguise

The dragon erupts from the disguise, destroying it. The explosive revelation deals 9d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in a 5-foot emanation with a DC 26 basic Reflex save. A creature that fails its save is [[condition.dazzled|dazzled]] for 1 round as it becomes covered in scraps from the disguise. Any creature sharing a space with the dragon after they erupt is pushed into the nearest empty space.
Draconic Frenzy
The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
Draconic Momentum
When the dragon scores a critical hit with a Strike, they recharge Smoke Breath.
Retract Body
The dragon retracts the targeted body part or twists away to avoid the attack, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
The dragon is hit or critically hit by an attack made by a creature the dragon can see
once per hour
Rushed Transformation

Using the aid of magic and an exhausting amount of effort, the dragon quickly reshapes their body into the form of a generic [[trait.humanoid|humanoid]] figure. This has the effects of [[spell.humanoid-form|humanoid form]] except that it lasts only 1 minute, and the dragon doesn't gain the +4 status bonus to [[skill.deception|Deception]] as the transformation makes use of the dragon's body to crudely mimic a humanoid form. The dragon can [[action.dismiss|Dismiss]] the effect. Whenever the effect ends, the dragon leaves behind scraps of magically conjured flesh, which could give away the dragon's presence.
Smoke Breath

The dragon unleashes a noxious cloud of smoke that deals 7d6 poison damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 26 basic Fortitude save). The smoke remains for 1 minute. This has the effects of [[spell.mist|mist]], except it fills the cone's area. The dragon can't use Smoke Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
Sneak Attack
The dragon's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] targets.
creature.young-conspirator-dragon.name: Young Conspirator Dragon
creature.young-diabolic-dragon.abilities: Any fire damage that a diabolic dragon deals, including fire damage from spells, is imbued with the unholy power of Hell to scorch the spirit as well. A creature takes [[trait.spirit|spirit]] damage instead of fire damage if that would be more detrimental to the creature (as determined by the GM). A diabolic dragon is immune to the diabolic fire of other diabolic dragons, the fire from [[spell.divine-immolation|divine immolation]], and similar effects.
The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Hellfire Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
The dragon unleashes a blast of infernal fire that deals 12d6 fire damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 30 basic Reflex save). The dragon can't use Hellfire Breath again for 1d4 rounds.

The dragon channels the rancor of Hell back through the body of their foe, overwhelming it with an infernal assault on the mind. The triggering creature takes 6d6 mental damage with a DC 30 basic Will save. [[trait.holy|Holy]] creatures use an outcome one degree of success worse than they roll on their saving throw.
The dragon is critically hit with a melee attack
Smoke doesn't impair the dragon's vision; they ignore the [[condition.concealed|concealed]] condition from smoke.
creature.young-diabolic-dragon.name: Young Diabolic Dragon
creature.young-empyreal-dragon.abilities: The dragon tosses their halo to a square within 90 feet. While the halo is deployed in this way, the dragon loses their inspiring presence aura, and the aura instead emanates from the halo with the same emanation radius. The dragon can Sustain to recall the halo from any distance. The halo is made of pure light—it doesn't occupy space and can't be targeted or destroyed in any way.
Divine power intercedes, preventing some of the damage. The dragon gains resistance 10 to all damage against the triggering attack.
The dragon is critically hit by an attack
The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Spirit Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.

The dragon chooses one effect to impose on creatures in their inspiring presence aura. The dragon can't use Halo Pulse again for 1d4 rounds.
- **Repulsion** Each creature must succeed at a DC 29 Fortitude save or be pushed until it's no longer in the aura.
- **Restoration** ([[trait.healing|healing]], [[trait.vitality|vitality]]) Each creature recovers 5d8 Hit Points.

20 feet. The mere sight of an empyreal dragon motivates other creatures. Creatures within the aura gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws and skill checks. The empyreal dragon can't gain the benefit of their own aura or other actions that use the aura, and they can choose to exclude any creatures from any benefit of the aura or action that uses the aura.
The dragon unleashes a blast of holy fire that deals 9d8 spirit damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 29 basic Reflex save). The dragon can't use Spirit Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
creature.young-empyreal-dragon.lore.3: Plane of Law and Good Lore
creature.young-empyreal-dragon.name: Young Empyreal Dragon
The dragon attempts to capture a portion of the spell's magic to feed themself. They attempt to counteract the spell (counteract rank 5, counteract modifier +20). If successful, the dragon is unaffected by the spell and regains one expended spontaneous spell slot; other subjects are affected by the spell normally.
The dragon succeeds or critically succeeds on a saving throw against a spell

The dragon unleashes a spray of magic-disrupting energies that deals 9d6 force damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 30 basic Reflex save). Creatures that fail become [[condition.stupefied|stupefied 1]] (stupefied 2 on a critical failure) for 1 minute. The dragon can't use Disruptive Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
Whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike, the dragon chooses to either recharge Disruptive Breath or regain one expended spontaneous spell slot.
The dragon's body is covered in riches (this is typically the case when the dragon is first encountered)

The dragon shakes their body aggressively, sending coins and other riches flying in every direction, dealing 6d10 bludgeoning damage with a DC 29 basic Reflex save to all creatures in a 30-foot emanation. The dragon's body is then no longer covered in riches.
The dragon's body isn't covered in riches and the dragon is adjacent to their hoard

The dragon Strides or [[action.burrow|Burrows]] through their hoard using their land Speed. They coat themself in coins, magic items, and other treasures. This contact with magical items revitalizes the dragon, causing them to regain one expended spontaneous spell slot. The dragon can move through other creatures while moving in this way. Creatures in the dragon's path, or above it if the dragon Burrows, must succeed at a DC 27 Reflex save or be pushed 10 feet (or pushed 20 feet and knocked [[condition.prone|prone]] on a critical failure).
creature.young-fortune-dragon.name: Young Fortune Dragon
creature.young-horned-dragon.abilities.d: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one horn Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Poison Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
creature.young-horned-dragon.abilities.f: The horned dragon ignores any difficult terrain caused by plants, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth. Even plants manipulated by magic don't impede their progress.
creature.young-horned-dragon.abilities.i: The dragon doesn't have a creature impaled on their horn

The dragon attempts to gore a foe. They Stride, then attempt a horn Strike. On a hit, the target becomes impaled on the dragon's horn. The creature is [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]] while on the horn (and can attempt to [[action.escape|Escape]] as normal). The dragon doesn't need to use additional actions to keep the impaled creature grabbed. If the dragon moves, they bring the grabbed creature along with them.
creature.young-horned-dragon.abilities.p: The dragon breathes a toxic cloud that deals 9d6 poison damage in a 40-foot cone (DC 25 basic Fortitude save). They can't use Poison Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
creature.young-horned-dragon.abilities.t: The dragon makes a tail Strike at the creature with a –2 penalty. If the Strike hits, the dragon disrupts the creature's action.
A creature within reach of the dragon's tail uses a [[trait.move|move]] action or leaves a square during a move action it's using
creature.young-horned-dragon.name: Young Horned Dragon
creature.young-mirage-dragon.abilities.c: The dragon can [[action.hide|Hide]] in natural environments even if they don't have cover.
creature.young-mirage-dragon.abilities.d: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Hallucinatory Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
creature.young-mirage-dragon.abilities.h: The dragon breathes a cloud that assaults the senses and deals 7d6 mental damage in a 30-foot cone (DC 27 Will save). A creature that fails its save is also [[condition.confused|confused]] for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure) and is then temporarily immune to being confused by Hallucinatory Breath for 1 hour. The dragon can't use Hallucinatory Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
creature.young-mirage-dragon.abilities.l: The dragon lunges their head forward, making a jaws Strike with an extended reach of 20 feet.
creature.young-mirage-dragon.abilities.s: The dragon flashes their iridescent scales at the triggering creature to throw off the attack. The dragon gains [[condition.concealed|concealment]] against the triggering attack.
The dragon is targeted with an attack
The dragon's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] targets.
creature.young-mirage-dragon.name: Young Mirage Dragon
creature.young-omen-dragon.abilities.cha: This fate is not set in stone. The attacker rolls the triggering attack twice and uses the worse result.
The dragon is targeted by an attack
creature.young-omen-dragon.abilities.des: The dragon breathes a translucent mist of potentialities that overwhelms creatures with visions of possible features, dealing 6d6 mental damage in a 20-foot cone (DC 25 Will save). A creature that fails its save is [[condition.slowed|slowed 1]] for 1 round (or slowed 2 on a critical failure) as it struggles with the visions. The dragon can't use Destiny Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
creature.young-omen-dragon.abilities.dra: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order.
The dragon recharges their Destiny Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
creature.young-omen-dragon.abilities.pro: The dragon or any ally can glimpse into the future through the dragon's wings in a process that requires 10 minutes of concentration. This casts a 4th-rank [[spell.augury|augury]] spell, except that the wings can predict results up to 1 day into the future and the dragon always speaks a few cryptic words related to the result of the prediction. The dragon can use their wings in this way only once per hour, and a given creature can seek a future in the wings only once per week.
creature.young-omen-dragon.abilities.unt: The dragon can choose to negate any [[trait.fortune|fortune]] or [[trait.misfortune|misfortune]] effects that would affect them; other creatures remain affected normally.
creature.young-omen-dragon.name: Young Omen Dragon
creature.zecui.abilities.dual-stab.name: Dual Stab
creature.zecui.abilities.dual-stab.text: The zecui makes two shortsword Strikes against an [[condition.immobilized|immobilized]] or [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] target. These strikes count towards the zecui's multiple attack penalty, but it doesn't increase until after the second attack.
creature.zecui.abilities.harden-chitin.t: The zecui fuses much of their chitin into a black metallic shell. They gain resistance 5 to all damage (except [[trait.mental|mental]] and [[trait.spirit|spirit]]) until they next take a [[trait.move|move]] action.
creature.zecui.abilities.preserve-prey.t: The zecui channels corrupt vitality into the triggering creature, which still goes [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]] but does not gain the [[condition.dying|dying]] condition. While that creature is unconscious, the residual energy attempts to counteract any [[trait.vitality|vitality]] spell healing that creature with a +15 counteract modifier.
A living creature within 30 feet is reduced to 0 Hit Points
creature.zecui.abilities.spit-mucus.name: Spit Mucus
creature.zecui.abilities.spit-mucus.text: A creature hit by the zecui's spit attack is [[condition.immobilized|immobilized]] by the larva-infested mucus and stuck to the nearest surface until it [[action.escape|Escapes]] (DC 25). While that creature is immobilized, it is exposed to zecui larvae at the end of each of its turns.
creature.zecui.abilities.zecui-larvae.te: **Saving Throw** DC 25 Fortitude; **Stage 1** visible lumps as the larvae move but no ill effect (1 day); **Stage 2** [[condition.drained|drained 1]] (1 day); **Stage 3** drained 2 (1 day); **Stage 4** drained 3 and [[condition.controlled|controlled]] by the zecui larva (1 day); **Stage 5** the creature dies and the adult zecui can emerge from the corpse as an Interact action

creature.zephyr-hawk.name: Zephyr Hawk
creature.zephyr-hawk.strikes.wing.name: wing
creature.zoaem.abilities.archons-protect: The ally gains resistance 3 to all damage against the triggering damage and the archon can make a Strike against the enemy.
An enemy damages the archon's ally and both are within 15 feet of the archon
creature.zoaem.abilities.behold.name: Behold!
creature.zoaem.abilities.behold.text: The zoaem's rings and wings move in a complex pattern, mesmerizing creatures in the zoaem's choice of a 10-foot emanation or a 5-foot burst within 60 feet. Each creature must succeed at a DC 17 Will save or be [[condition.fascinated|fascinated]] with the zoaem for 1 minute and [[condition.stunned|stunned 1]] (or stunned for 1 round on a critical failure).
The zoaem shines an intense light of truth, as [[spell.revealing-light|revealing light]] but in a 60-foot line. Against creatures affected by this light, the zoaem and their allies gain a +1 status bonus to damage rolls and [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] checks. The zoaem can't use Light of Truth again for 1d4 rounds.
creature.zoaem.name: Zoaem
creature.zoaem.strikes.eye-ray.name: eye ray

creature.zombie-brute.strikes.fist.name: fist

creature.zombie-hulk.abilities.slow.name: Slow
creature.zombie-hulk.abilities.slow.text: A zombie is permanently [[condition.slowed|slowed 1]] and can't use reactions.

creature.zombie-shambler.name: Zombie Shambler
creature.zyss-serpentfolk.abilities.serp: **Saving Throw** DC 16 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 1d4 poison damage and [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled 1]] (1 round); **Stage 2** 2d4 poison damage and enfeebled 1 (1 round)
creature.zyss-serpentfolk.abilities.thin: Zyss serpentfolk recover slowly from injuries. When they take physical damage from a critical hit, they gain 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]]. They take a –2 circumstance penalty to flat checks to recover from persistent damage and saving throws against afflictions.
creature.zyss-serpentfolk.name: Zyss Serpentfolk
creature.zyss-serpentfolk.saves.note: Will +4 status vs. [[trait.mental|mental]]; +1 status to all saves vs. [[trait.magical|magic]]
feat.a-home-in-every-port.name: A Home in Every Port
feat.a-home-in-every-port.text: You have a reputation in towns and villages you've visited, and residents are always willing to open their doors to you. When in a town or village, during downtime, you can spend 8 hours to locate a resident willing to provide lodging for you and up to six allies for up to 24 hours at no charge. The standard of living within the acquired lodging is comfortable, and square meals are provided at no cost. After 24 hours, you must pay standard prices for further lodging and meals or use this feat again to find a new resident willing to host you.
feat.absorb-strength.name: Absorb Strength
feat.absorb-strength.text: You consume a piece of your enemy, absorbing their strength. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to the enemy's level that last for 1 minute.
feat.absorb-strength.trigger: You are adjacent to an enemy's corpse who has been dead for no longer than 1 minute.
feat.absorb-toxin.name: Absorb Toxin
feat.absorb-toxin.prereq.0: You are not immune to diseases or poisons
feat.absorb-toxin.text: Your skin readily absorbs poison and can consciously draw toxins into your body to spare others. Attempt a counteract check against the triggering effect; your counteract rank equals half your level (rounded up), and for the roll use either your class DC – 10 or your spellcasting attribute modifier plus your spellcasting proficiency bonus. If you counteract the triggering effect, you end the effect for all other creatures in the area; however, you must still save against the effect with a –2 penalty to the initial save.
feat.absorb-toxin.trigger: You attempt a saving throw against a disease or poison effect that affects an area.
feat.accompany.name: Accompany
feat.accompany.text: You use your performance to supplement an ally’s spellcasting, providing magical energy for their spell in their stead. Attempt a Performance check, using a very high DC for the ally’s level (see the difficulty class rules), and either spend a Focus Point (if the triggering spell is a focus spell) or expend a spell slot at least 1 rank higher than the triggering spell. If you succeed at your Performance check, your ally’s spell doesn’t cost the Focus Point or spell slot that ally would normally need to spend.
feat.accompany.trigger: An ally within 30 feet Casts a Spell
feat.accursed-claws.name: Accursed Claws
feat.accursed-claws.text: Your claws carry your mother’s hag magic. When you critically hit with a claw [[action.strike|Strike]], the target takes an additional 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent mental damage]].
feat.acquired-tolerance.name: Acquired Tolerance
feat.acquired-tolerance.text: A small amount of poison taken at nonlethal doses, can help the body build up resistance against a more deadly dosage. Reroll the triggering check and use the second result. Once you use Acquired Tolerance, you can continue to use it against the same type of poison that day, but you can't use it against a different type of poison until after you make your next daily preparations. For instance, if you used the reaction on a save against [[item.giant-scorpion-venom|giant scorpion venom]], you could use it again against giant scorpion venom even if it came from a different source, but you couldn't use it against [[item.wyvern-poison|wyvern poison]].
feat.acquired-tolerance.trigger: You fail a save against a poison.
feat.acrobat-dedication.name: Acrobat Dedication
feat.acrobat-dedication.text: You become an expert in [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]]. At 7th level, you become a master in Acrobatics, and at 15th level, you become legendary in Acrobatics. Whenever you critically succeed at an Acrobatics check to [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] an enemy's space, you don't treat the enemy's space as difficult terrain.
feat.acrobatic-performer.name: Acrobatic Performer
feat.acrobatic-performer.text: You're an incredible acrobat, evoking wonder and enrapturing audiences with your prowess. You can roll an Acrobatics check instead of a [[skill.performance|Performance]] check when using the [[action.perform|Perform]] action. If you are trained in both Acrobatics and Performance, you gain a +1 circumstances bonus on Acrobatics checks made to Perform.
feat.acute-scent.name: Acute Scent
feat.acute-scent.text: When your anger is heightened, your sense of smell improves. While you're raging, you gain imprecise scent with a range of 30 feet.
feat.acute-vision.name: Acute Vision
feat.acute-vision.text: When you are raging, your visual senses improve, granting you darkvision.
feat.adapted-cantrip.name: Adapted Cantrip
feat.adapted-cantrip.text:
Through study of multiple magical traditions, you’ve altered a spell to suit your spellcasting style. Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own. If you prepare spells, you can choose this spell when you prepare your cantrips, in addition to your other options. If you have a spell repertoire, replace one of your cantrips known with the chosen spell. You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class’s tradition.

If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.
feat.adaptive-adept.name: Adaptive Adept
feat.adaptive-adept.text: You’ve continued adapting your magic to blend your class’s tradition with your adapted tradition. Choose a cantrip or 1st-rank spell from the same magical tradition as your cantrip from [[feat.adapted-cantrip|Adapted Cantrip]]. You gain that spell, adding it to your spell options just like the cantrip from Adapted Cantrip. You can cast this spell as a spell of your class’s magical tradition. If you choose a 1st-rank spell, you don’t gain access to the heightened versions of that spell, meaning you can’t prepare them if you prepare spells and you can’t learn them or select the spell as a signature spell if you have a spell repertoire.
feat.additional-companion.name: Additional Companion
feat.additional-companion.text:
Another animal joins you in your travels. It is a young animal companion that has the [[trait.minion|minion]] trait. See Beastmaster Animal Companions for rules on how having multiple animal companions works.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, gaining an additional animal companion each time, to a maximum of four total companions from all sources.
feat.additional-lore.name: Additional Lore
feat.additional-lore.text:
Your knowledge has expanded to encompass a new field. Choose a Lore skill subcategory. You become trained in it. At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you must select a new subcategory of Lore and you gain the additional skill increases to that subcategory for the listed levels.
feat.additional-recollection.name: Additional Recollection
feat.additional-recollection.text: You scan the battlefield quickly, remembering critical details about multiple opponents you face. You immediately attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about a different creature you can perceive.
feat.additional-recollection.trigger: You succeed or critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge on your hunted prey
feat.adopted-ancestry.name: Adopted Ancestry
feat.adopted-ancestry.text: You’re fully immersed in another ancestry’s culture and traditions, whether born into them, earned through rite of passage, or bonded through a deep friendship or romance. Choose a common ancestry or another ancestry to which you have access. You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character’s own ancestry, as long as the ancestry feats don’t require any physiological feature that you lack, as determined by the GM.
feat.adrenaline-rush.name: Adrenaline Rush
feat.adrenaline-rush.text: In the heat of battle, you are capable of amazing feats of strength. While you are raging, increase your encumbered and maximum Bulk limits by 2; you also gain a +1 status bonus to [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] checks to lift heavy objects, [[action.escape|Escape]], and [[action.force-open|Force Open]].
feat.advanced-alchemy.name: Advanced Alchemy
feat.advanced-alchemy.text: You gain the advanced alchemy benefits, and you can create 4 alchemical consumables during your daily preparations.
feat.advanced-arcana.name: Advanced Arcana
feat.advanced-arcana.text:
You gain one wizard feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your wizard level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another wizard feat.
feat.advanced-blood-potency.name: Advanced Blood Potency
feat.advanced-blood-potency.text:
You gain one sorcerer feat. For the purpose of prerequisites, your sorcerer level is half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you do, you gain another sorcerer feat.
feat.advanced-bloodline.name: Advanced Bloodline
feat.advanced-bloodline.text: You draw more power from your bloodline. You gain the advanced bloodline spell associated with your bloodline.
feat.advanced-concoction.name: Advanced Concoction
feat.advanced-concoction.text:
You gain one alchemist feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your alchemist level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another alchemist feat.
feat.advanced-deduction.name: Advanced Deduction
feat.advanced-deduction.text:
You gain one investigator feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your investigator level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another investigator feat.
feat.advanced-deitys-domain.name: Advanced Deity's Domain
feat.advanced-deitys-domain.text: Through your conviction, you have glimpsed the deeper secrets of your deity's domain. You gain an advanced domain spell from the domain you chose with Deity's Domain as a devotion spell.
feat.advanced-devotion.name: Advanced Devotion
feat.advanced-devotion.text:
You gain one champion feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your champion level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another champion feat.
feat.advanced-dogma.name: Advanced Dogma
feat.advanced-dogma.text:
You gain one cleric feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your cleric level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another cleric feat.
feat.advanced-domain.name: Advanced Domain
feat.advanced-domain.text:
Your prayers have unlocked deeper secrets of your deity’s domain. You gain an advanced domain spell from one of your domains for which you have an initial domain spell.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, you must select a different advanced domain spell.
feat.advanced-efficient-alchemy.name: Advanced Efficient Alchemy
feat.advanced-efficient-alchemy.text: You make an even-larger batch of alchemical items each morning. Increase the maximum number of items you can create with advanced alchemy to 8 + your Intelligence modifier, or to 10 + your Intelligence modifier if you're 16th level or higher.
feat.advanced-first-aid.name: Advanced First Aid
feat.advanced-first-aid.text: You use your medical training to ameliorate sickness or assuage fears. When you use Medicine to Administer First Aid, instead of Stabilizing a character or Stopping Bleeding, you can reduce an ally’s frightened or sickened condition by 2, or remove either of those conditions entirely on a critical success. You can remove only one condition at a time. The DC for the Medicine check is usually the DC of the effect that caused the condition.
feat.advanced-flair.name: Advanced Flair
feat.advanced-flair.text:
You gain one swashbuckler feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your swashbuckler level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another swashbuckler feat.
feat.advanced-fury.name: Advanced Fury
feat.advanced-fury.text:
You gain one barbarian feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your barbarian level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another barbarian feat.
feat.advanced-general-training.name: Advanced General Training
feat.advanced-general-training.text:
Over the long course of your adventuring life, your adaptability has let you pick up numerous useful abilities. You gain a general feat of 7th level or lower. You must meet the feat’s prerequisites.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a different feat each time.
feat.advanced-herbalism.name: Advanced Herbalism
feat.advanced-herbalism.text:
Your herbalist talents continue to grow with use and you have become potent at making even more remedies from less. You can create up to 6 herbal items per day with advanced alchemy.

**Special** At 10th level or higher, you can select this feat a second time to increase the number to 8.
feat.advanced-hunters-trick.name: Advanced Hunter's Trick
feat.advanced-hunters-trick.text:
You gain one ranger feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your ranger level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another ranger feat.
feat.advanced-kata.name: Advanced Kata
feat.advanced-kata.text:
You gain one monk feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your monk level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another monk feat.
feat.advanced-maneuver.name: Advanced Maneuver
feat.advanced-maneuver.text:
You gain a fighter feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your fighter level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another fighter feat.
feat.advanced-monastic-weaponry.name: Advanced Monastic Weaponry
feat.advanced-monastic-weaponry.text: Your rigorous training regimen allows you to wield complex weaponry with ease. For the purposes of proficiency, you treat advanced [[trait.monk|monk]] weapons as if they were martial monk weapons.
feat.advanced-muses-whispers.name: Advanced Muse's Whispers
feat.advanced-muses-whispers.text:
You gain one bard feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your bard level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another bard feat.
feat.advanced-mysteries.name: Advanced Mysteries
feat.advanced-mysteries.text:
You gain one oracle feat. For meeting its prerequisites, your oracle level is equal to half your level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you gain another oracle feat.
feat.advanced-poisoncraft.name: Advanced Poisoncraft
feat.advanced-poisoncraft.text:
You can create up to 6 poisons per day with advanced alchemy.

**Special** At 10th level or higher, you can select this feat a second time to increase the number to 8.
feat.advanced-qi-spells.name: Advanced Qi Spells
feat.advanced-qi-spells.text:
Your talent at controlling your qi has reached new heights. You gain [[spell.qi-blast|_qi blast_]], [[spell.shrink-the-span|_shrink the span_]], or another 3rd-rank qi spell you have access to.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.
feat.advanced-revelation.name: Advanced Revelation
feat.advanced-revelation.text: Divine power reveals greater mysteries to you. You learn the advanced revelation spell associated with your mystery.
feat.advanced-school-spell.name: Advanced School Spell
feat.advanced-school-spell.text: You gain access to the advanced teachings of your arcane institution, learning a powerful new school spell. You gain the advanced school spell for your arcane school.
feat.advanced-trickery.name: Advanced Trickery
feat.advanced-trickery.text:
You gain one rogue feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your rogue level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another rogue feat.
feat.advanced-warden.name: Advanced Warden
feat.advanced-warden.text:
You unlock more powerful primal spells. You gain your choice of one warden spell from the advanced warden spells (or another you have access to).

**Special** You can take this feat multiple times, choosing a different advanced warden spell each time.
feat.advanced-weapon-training.name: Advanced Weapon Training
feat.advanced-weapon-training.text: You’ve studied the art of wielding an advanced weapon. Choose a weapon group. You gain proficiency with all advanced weapons in that group as if they were martial weapons of their weapon group.
feat.advanced-wilding.name: Advanced Wilding
feat.advanced-wilding.text:
You gain one druid feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your druid level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another druid feat.
feat.advanced-witchcraft.name: Advanced Witchcraft
feat.advanced-witchcraft.text:
You gain one witch feat. For the purpose of meeting its prerequisites, your witch level is equal to half your character level.

**Special** l You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you gain another witch feat.
feat.advantageous-assault.name: Advantageous Assault
feat.advantageous-assault.text:
After compromising your enemy’s movement, you deliver a more deadly blow. Make a Strike against a creature that is grabbed, prone, or restrained. You gain a circumstance bonus to damage on this Strike equal to the number of weapon damage dice, or that number + 2 if you’re wielding the weapon in two hands. The Strike gains the following failure effect.

**Failure** You deal damage to the target equal to the number of weapon damage dice, or that number + 2 if you're wielding the weapon in two hands. This damage has the same damage type as the weapon.
feat.aerial-piledriver.name: Aerial Piledriver
feat.aerial-piledriver.text:
Heaving both yourself and your opponent into the air, you bring them crashing to the ground. Make an unarmed melee Strike against the creature you have [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]] or [[condition.restrained|restrained]]. This Strike deals 1d6 additional damage per weapon damage die, and it has the following additional effects on a success, failure, and critical failure.

**Success** The target lands [[condition.prone|prone]].

**Failure** You lose your grip on the target, and it is no longer grabbed or restrained by you.

**Critical Failure** You lose both your grip on the target and your balance. You fall prone, and the target is no longer grabbed or restrained by you.
feat.aerobatics-mastery.name: Aerobatics Mastery
feat.aerobatics-mastery.text: You move with grace in flight and can perform amazing aerial stunts. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Acrobatics checks to [[action.maneuver-in-flight|Maneuver in Flight]] and can combine two maneuvers into a single action, such as reversing direction while making a steep ascent or descent or hovering in gale-force winds. The DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 5. If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you can combine three such maneuvers into a single action; the DC of the Acrobatics check is equal to the DC of the most difficult maneuver + 10. Regardless of the combination, these maneuvers rarely allow you to move farther than your fly Speed.
feat.affliction-mercy.name: Affliction Mercy
feat.affliction-mercy.text: The divine grace that flows through you grants reprieve from an affliction. Add mercy of recuperation to the types of mercy you can provide, allowing you to counteract an affliction instead of an effect causing a condition (typically an affliction is a [[trait.curse|curse]], [[trait.disease|disease]], or [[trait.poison|poison]]).
feat.affliction-resistance.name: Affliction Resistance
feat.affliction-resistance.text: Your diet has strengthened you against diseases and poisons. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [[trait.disease|diseases]] and [[trait.poison|poisons]]. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the [[class.fighter|battle hardened fighter class feature]]), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.
feat.after-you.name: After You
feat.after-you.text: You allow your foes to make the first move in a show of incredible confidence. You don't roll initiative; instead you voluntarily go last. You gain panache. If more than one character uses this ability or another ability to go last, use the normal rules for resolving a tie: NPCs and monsters act before PCs, and within those groups, the creatures can choose whichever order they want.
feat.ageless-patience.name: Ageless Patience
feat.ageless-patience.text:
You work at a pace born from longevity that enhances your thoroughness. You can voluntarily spend twice as much time as normal on a Perception check or skill check that takes 1 action or longer. If you do, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the check and don't automatically reduce your degree of success on a natural 1 (you get a critical failure only if your result is 10 lower than the DC). For example, you could get these benefits if you spent 2 actions to [[action.seek|Seek]], which normally takes 1 action. You can get these benefits during exploration by taking twice as long exploring as normal, or in downtime by spending twice as much downtime.

The GM might determine a situation doesn't grant you a benefit if a delay would be directly counterproductive to your success, such as a tense negotiation with an impatient creature.
feat.aggravating-scratch.name: Aggravating Scratch
feat.aggravating-scratch.text: Your claws carry an irritant that is harmless to you but can be damaging to others. Your claw Strikes deal an additional 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent poison damage]] on a critical hit.
feat.aggressive-block.name: Aggressive Block
feat.aggressive-block.text: You push back as you block, knocking your foe away or off balance. You use your shield to push the triggering creature, either automatically Shoving it 5 feet or causing it to become off-guard until the start of your next turn. The triggering creature chooses whether to be moved or become off-guard. If it chooses to be moved, you choose the direction. If the Shove would cause it to hit a solid object, enter a square of difficult terrain, or enter another creature’s space, it must become off-guard instead of being moved.
feat.aggressive-block.trigger: You use the Shield Block reaction, and the opponent that triggered Shield Block is adjacent to you and is your size or smaller
feat.agile-grace.name: Agile Grace
feat.agile-grace.text: Your graceful moves with agile weapons are beyond compare. Your multiple attack penalty with agile weapons and agile unarmed attacks becomes –3 for your second attack and –6 for subsequent attacks (rather than –4 and –8).
feat.agile-maneuvers.name: Agile Maneuvers
feat.agile-maneuvers.text: Your easily maneuver against your foes. Your [[action.disarm|Disarm]], [[action.grapple|Grapple]], [[action.reposition|Reposition]], [[action.shove|Shove]], and [[action.trip|Trip]] actions have a lower multiple attack penalty. Even if your weapon or [[trait.unarmed|unarmed]] attack doesn't have the [[trait.agile|agile]] trait, the penalty is –4 if the action is your second attack on your turn, or –8 if it's your third or subsequent attack. If your weapon or unarmed attack is agile and you have panache, the penalty is reduced further, to –3 if it's the second attack on your turn or –6 if it's the third or subsequent.
feat.agonizing-rebuke.name: Agonizing Rebuke
feat.agonizing-rebuke.text: When you terrorize your enemies, you also cause them painful mental distress. When you successfully [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]] an enemy, that enemy takes 1d4 mental damage at the start of each of its turns. This effect ends if the creature loses the [[condition.frightened|frightened]] condition, if it is more than 30 feet away from you, or if 1 minute passes, whichever comes first. If you have master proficiency in Intimidation, the damage increases to 2d4, and if you have legendary proficiency, the damage increases to 3d4.
feat.alchemical-assessment.name: Alchemical Assessment
feat.alchemical-assessment.text: You can identify alchemical items quickly. When using the Crafting skill to [[action.identify-alchemy|Identify Alchemy]] on an [[trait.alchemical|alchemical]] item you hold, you can do so as a single action, rather than spending 10 minutes.
feat.alchemical-crafting.name: Alchemical Crafting
feat.alchemical-crafting.text: You can use the Craft activity to create alchemical items. When you select this feat, you immediately add the formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items to your [[item.formula-book-blank|formula book]].
feat.alchemical-discoveries.name: Alchemical Discoveries
feat.alchemical-discoveries.text: You've devoted extra time in the lab to improve your knowledge of alchemy. You learn the formulas for two [[trait.alchemical|alchemical items]] each time you level up instead of one; these must still be elixirs or tools. The number of versatile vials you can create each day increases by one if you're an expert in [[skill.crafting|Crafting]], two if you're a master, or three if you're legendary.
feat.alchemical-familiar.name: Alchemical Familiar
feat.alchemical-familiar.text: You have used alchemy to create life, a simple creature formed from alchemical materials, reagents, and a bit of your own blood. You gain a familiar, which has the construct familiar ability; this is permanent, doesn't require the familiar to have the tough familiar ability, and doesn't count against your usual limit of familiar abilities (typically 2). The familiar uses your Intelligence modifier to determine its Perception, [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]], and [[skill.stealth|Stealth]] modifiers.
feat.alchemical-power.name: Alchemical Power
feat.alchemical-power.text: You become an expert in the alchemist class DC. When you create an infused alchemical item that allows a saving throw, you can change its DC to your class DC.
feat.alchemical-revivification.name: Alchemical Revivification
feat.alchemical-revivification.text: If you die while under the effect of at least one [[trait.elixir|elixir]], the alchemical compounds in your bloodstream bring you back to life at the start of your next turn. You're affected by an [[item.elixir-of-rejuvenation|elixir of rejuvenation]], then a [[item.elixir-of-life-true|true elixir of life]], then your choice of a [[item.bestial-mutagen-major|major bestial mutagen]], [[item.juggernaut-mutagen-major|major juggernaut mutagen]], or [[item.quicksilver-mutagen-major|major quicksilver mutagen]] as though you just imbibed it. These automatic reactions don't get any special benefits you add when creating or using these items. Because you died, all other alchemical compounds in your bloodstream are inert. After being revived, you're temporarily immune to Alchemical Rejuvenation for 1d4 hours.
feat.alchemical-scholar.name: Alchemical Scholar
feat.alchemical-scholar.text: You gain the [[feat.alchemical-crafting|Alchemical Crafting]] feat. If you would automatically gain that feat (from your background or the alchemist class, for example), you instead gain a different 1st-level Crafting skill feat. Add an additional common 1st-level [[trait.alchemical|alchemical]] formula to your formula book when you take this feat. Each time you gain a level beyond 1st, add one common alchemical formula of that level to your formula book.
feat.alchemist-dedication.name: Alchemist Dedication
feat.alchemist-dedication.text:
You put your alchemical interest into practice. You become trained in alchemical bombs, the alchemist class DC, and Crafting; if you were already trained in [[skill.crafting|Crafting]], you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You gain the Quick Alchemy benefits, creating up to 4 versatile vials during your daily preparations. Add the formulas for four additional common alchemical items to your formula book, in addition to those you gain from [[feat.alchemical-crafting|Alchemical Crafting]].
feat.align-qi.name: Align Qi
feat.align-qi.text: The power of your qi soothes your wounds and energizes you for battle. You regain Hit Points equal to your level plus your Wisdom modifier.
feat.align-qi.trigger: You [[action.cast-a-spell|Cast a Spell]] that has the [[trait.monk|monk]] trait.
feat.all-in-my-head.name: All in my Head
feat.all-in-my-head.text: Using your occult connections and incredible powers of persuasion, you convince yourself that the triggering damage is a figment of your imagination. The damage changes from its usual damage type to mental damage, and the damaging effect gains the nonlethal trait. You can’t use this reaction if you are immune to mental effects or mental damage.
feat.all-in-my-head.trigger: You would take damage from a Strike or spell that doesn’t have the death trait or otherwise cause instant death (such as disintegrate)
feat.allegro.name: Allegro
feat.allegro.text: You can quicken your allies with a fast-paced performance. You learn the [[spell.allegro|_allegro_]] [[trait.composition|composition]] cantrip.
feat.allys-shelter.name: Ally's Shelter
feat.allys-shelter.text: You follow your allies' example. Roll the save using an adjacent ally's modifier for that type of saving throw instead of your own.
feat.allys-shelter.trigger: You attempt a saving throw while adjacent to one or more allies, but you haven't rolled yet.
feat.alter-admixture.name: Alter Admixture
feat.alter-admixture.requirements: You are holding or wearing an [[item.alchemists-toolkit|alchemist's toolkit]].
feat.alter-admixture.text: Sometimes, you need to adapt your alchemical mixtures to new situations. In a process that takes 10 minutes, you change an item you created with advanced alchemy into a similar item. You can change an alchemical bomb into another type of alchemical bomb, an elixir into another type of elixir, or a poison into another type of poison. If it's unclear whether two alchemical consumables are similar, the GM decides. You must know the formula for the new item, and the new item must be of the same or lower item level than the original item. The new item still keeps the [[trait.infused|infused]] trait, and it remains potent as long as the original item would have.
feat.ambush-hunter.name: Ambush Hunter
feat.ambush-hunter.text: You are always searching for the perfect opportunity to ambush your enemies. You can perform the [[action.scout|Scout]] exploration activity at the same time as the [[action.avoid-notice|Avoid Notice]] exploration activity.
feat.analyze-idiolect.name: Analyze Idiolect
feat.analyze-idiolect.text: You break down a specific individual’s idiolect, memorizing their speech mannerisms and habits. If you interact with someone for at least 10 minutes, when you later attempt to [[action.impersonate|Impersonate]] that individual, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your [[skill.deception|Deception]] checks and DCs. Due to the intense character study required, if you Analyze Idiolect again, it replaces any previous idiolect you memorized.
feat.analyze-weakness.name: Analyze Weakness
feat.analyze-weakness.requirements: You have identified a creature with Recall Knowledge
feat.analyze-weakness.text:
Your knowledge of a creature’s physiology helps you attack with pinpoint accuracy. You carefully study a creature that you’ve identified to scope out particularly weak points in its positioning or physical form. The next time you deal sneak attack damage to the chosen creature with a Strike before the end of your turn, add an additional 2d6 precision damage.

At 11th level, the additional damage becomes 3d6, and at 17th level it becomes 4d6.
feat.ancestors-rage.name: Ancestor's Rage
feat.ancestors-rage.text: You transform into an enormous, otherworldly hyena. You can cast [[spell.animal-form|_animal form_]] (canine form only) once per day as a 5th-rank occult innate spell.
feat.ancestral-longevity.name: Ancestral Longevity
feat.ancestral-longevity.text: You have accumulated a vast array of lived knowledge over the years. During your daily preparations, you can reflect upon your life experiences to gain the trained proficiency rank in one skill of your choice. This proficiency lasts until you prepare again. Since this proficiency is temporary, you can’t use it as a prerequisite for a skill increase or a permanent character option like a feat.
feat.ancestral-paragon.name: Ancestral Paragon
feat.ancestral-paragon.text: Whether through instinct, study, or magic, you feel a deeper connection to your ancestry. You gain a 1st-level ancestry feat.
feat.ancestral-suspicion.name: Ancestral Suspicion
feat.ancestral-suspicion.text: Long-lived elves have seen civilizations rise and fall, often at the hands of outside forces. As a result, they have developed a wariness of others who might seek to influence or control them. You've been trained to resist such manipulation, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would make you controlled, such as [[spell.dominate|_dominate_]], and to Perception checks to [[action.sense-motive|Sense Motive]] when trying to determine if a creature is under the influence of such an effect. When you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead.
feat.anchoring-roots.name: Anchoring Roots
feat.anchoring-roots.text:
Small roots sprout from your feet, steadying you as you move. You gain the [[feat.steady-balance|Steady Balance]] skill feat, even if you aren’t trained in [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]], and you can use the Anchor action.

**Anchor** {1a} **Requirements** You’re on a solid surface; **Effect** You send your roots into or across the ground, making it harder for you to stumble. Until you move, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to [[action.reposition|Reposition]], [[action.shove|Shove]], or [[action.trip|Trip]] you (or a +4 circumstance bonus if you’re a [[heritage.root-leshy|root leshy]]). This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to move you or knock you [[condition.prone|prone]]. If an effect forces you to move, you move only half the normal distance, as some of the effort goes to tearing loose the roots.
feat.angel-of-death.name: Angel of Death
feat.angel-of-death.text: All your Strikes against a creature you have Marked for Death have the [[trait.death|death]] trait, causing the mark to be instantly killed when reduced to 0 Hit Points. In addition, if the creature is killed this way, attempts to communicate with it, return it to life, turn it into an undead, or otherwise disturb its afterlife fail unless the effect's counteract rank is higher than half your level rounded up, or originates from an artifact or a deity. Use the level you were when you killed the creature, even if your level is higher at the time the attempt was made.
feat.angelkin.name: Angelkin
feat.angelkin.text: You descend from an angel, a winged messenger from the Plane of Good or one of the other celestial realms. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [[skill.society|Society]]. If you would automatically become trained in Society (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You know the Empyrean language, and you gain the [[feat.multilingual|Multilingual]] skill feat.
feat.animal-accomplice.name: Animal Accomplice
feat.animal-accomplice.text: You build a rapport with an animal, which becomes magically bonded to you. You gain a familiar. The type of animal is up to you, but most gnomes choose animals with a burrow Speed.
feat.animal-companion.name: Animal Companion
feat.animal-companion.text:
You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you on your adventures and obeys any simple commands you give it to the best of its abilities. See Animal Companions for more information.

**[[class.ranger|Ranger]]**: When you [[action.hunt-prey|Hunt Prey]], your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one.
feat.animal-elocutionist.name: Animal Elocutionist
feat.animal-elocutionist.text: You hear animal sounds as conversations instead of unintelligent noise, and you can respond in turn. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [[skill.diplomacy|Diplomacy]] skill with animals. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [[action.make-an-impression|Make an Impression]] on animals.
feat.animal-empathy-druid.name: Animal Empathy
feat.animal-empathy-druid.text: You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.
feat.animal-empathy-ranger.name: Animal Empathy
feat.animal-empathy-ranger.text: You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You can use Diplomacy to Make an Impression on animals and to make very simple Requests of them. In most cases, wild animals will give you time to make your case.
feat.animal-skin.name: Animal Skin
feat.animal-skin.text: Your proficiency in unarmored defense increases to expert. When you are raging and unarmored, your skin transforms into a thick hide. You gain a +2 item bonus to AC (+3 if you have the [[class.barbarian|greater juggernaut class feature]]). The thickness of your hide gives you a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +3. This item bonus to AC is cumulative with armor potency runes on your [[item.explorers-clothing|explorer's clothing]], [[spell.mystic-armor|_mystic armor_]], and bands of force.
feat.animalistic-brutality.name: Animalistic Brutality
feat.animalistic-brutality.text: You deepen the connection into your animal instincts. Your unarmed attack from bestial rage gains one of the following traits until you stop raging: [[trait.backswing|backswing]], [[trait.forceful|forceful]], [[trait.parry|parry]], [[trait.razing|razing]], or [[trait.sweep|sweep]]. You can't use this ability again until the next time you Rage. You can choose a different trait each time you use Animalistic Brutality
feat.annihilating-swing.name: Annihilating Swing
feat.annihilating-swing.text:
You have embraced brute destructive power. You make a melee Strike that ignores any resistances the target has. If you target a solid unattended object or surface with your Strike, you might automatically destroy it without an attack roll. If you target any object or surface with Hardness 20 or less that isn't a magic item or the effect of a spell, you destroy it.

If the target object or surface is a magic item or the effect of a spell, you attempt to counteract it using your attack bonus with the Strike for the counteract check. Your counteract rank is 10th. On a successful counteract check, you destroy the object or surface unless it has Hardness greater than 20, in an artifact, or is similarly difficult to destroy.

You destroy up to a 5-foot cube of an object or surface larger than Medium.
feat.annotate-composition.name: Annotate Composition
feat.annotate-composition.text:
By putting composition to paper, you can create a source of stirring words or song that others can read and understand. You spend 10 minutes and 1 Focus Point to transpose a composition spell on a special scroll that you or another creature can later activate. This composition spell must take a single action to cast. If the chosen composition spell requires a Performance check as part of the casting, the GM rolls this check as a secret check when you annotate your score. If you have fortissimo composition or lingering composition, you can also use one of those spells to modify the annotated composition, provided the annotated composition can benefit from the modification. The GM rolls the secret Performance check. If you do, you spend an additional Focus Point, even if the secret check fails.

Any creature that can read the language you used when annotating your composition can Activate the Item by spending a single action, which has the concentrate trait. This produces the effects of the composition as though the activating creature had Cast the Spell.

A composition you create this way loses its power the next time you make your daily preparations. While the composition is in your possession, you can render it inert using a single action that has the concentrate trait. You can’t regain the Focus Points you spent to create the annotated composition until it is activated or loses its magic.
feat.anoint-ally.name: Anoint Ally
feat.anoint-ally.text: You forge a mystical connection with an ally using a drop of your blood, allowing them to benefit from your magic. You place a blood rune on an adjacent ally that lasts for 1 minute. When you or an ally would gain a blood magic effect, you can forgo it, granting it to the anointed ally instead, even if they weren't a target of your spell. You can anoint only one ally at a time; if you place another rune, your previous designation ends.
feat.antagonize.name: Antagonize
feat.antagonize.text: Your taunts and threats earn your foes' ire. When you successfully [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]] a creature, its [[condition.frightened|frightened]] condition can't decrease to less than 1 at the end of its turn until it either uses a hostile action against you or can no longer observe or sense you for at least 1 round.
feat.anthemic-performance.name: Anthemic Performance
feat.anthemic-performance.text: Your music, speech, or other performance inspires your allies to dive into battle. You gain the [[spell.courageous-anthem|_courageous anthem_]] composition cantrip.
feat.anthropomorphic-shape.name: Anthropomorphic Shape
feat.anthropomorphic-shape.text: Humanoids' supposed place apart from animals is folly—taking on their forms just requires some extra practice. You add the shapes listed in [[spell.humanoid-form|_humanoid form_]] to your untamed form list.
feat.anticipate-ambush.name: Anticipate Ambush
feat.anticipate-ambush.text: You keep watch for any hidden creatures or dangerous sites, moving at half your travel Speed. If you’re Anticipating an Ambush at the start of an encounter, you roll a Perception check for initiative, and all enemies rolling Stealth for initiative take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Stealth checks.
feat.arcane-breadth.name: Arcane Breadth
feat.arcane-breadth.text: Your thorough studies allow you to cast more arcane spells each day. Increase the spell slots you gain from wizard archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest wizard spell slots.
feat.arcane-dragonblood.name: Arcane Dragonblood
feat.arcane-dragonblood.text: You descend from a dragon that wields mastery of their magical abilities, such as a fortune dragon or mirage dragon. As such, you can instinctively grasp the intricacies of magic. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [[skill.arcana|Arcana]]. If you would automatically become trained in Arcana (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the [[feat.arcane-sense|Arcane Sense]] skill feat. If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an arcane dragon.
feat.arcane-evolution.name: Arcane Evolution
feat.arcane-evolution.text: Your arcane legacy allows you to perceive how magic affects everything. You become trained in one skill of your choice. Additionally, you can use arcane arts to tinker with your selection of spells. During your daily preparations, you can choose one spell in your spell repertoire to be a signature spell that day. You can use the [[action.learn-a-spell|Learn a Spell]] activity to add more arcane spells to the list you choose from, but if you prepare a spell that isn't in your repertoire, you temporarily add it to your repertoire at the spell rank of your choice instead of making it a signature spell.
feat.arcane-school-spell.name: Arcane School Spell
feat.arcane-school-spell.text: You gain your school’s initial school spell. If you don’t already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus by studying.
feat.arcane-sense.name: Arcane Sense
feat.arcane-sense.text: Your study of magic allows you to instinctively sense its presence. You can cast 1st-rank detect magic at will as an arcane innate spell. If you’re a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you’re legendary, it is heightened to 4th rank.
feat.archaeologist-dedication.name: Archaeologist Dedication
feat.archaeologist-dedication.text: You are a student of peoples and their histories, and are in constant pursuit of knowledge and artifacts from the past. You become an expert in [[skill.society|Society]] and [[skill.thievery|Thievery]], and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] about ancient history, peoples, and cultures.
feat.archaeologists-luck.name: Archaeologist's Luck
feat.archaeologists-luck.text: You are more than just skillful; your drive to find the secrets of the past manifests as a strange kind of luck. Reroll the failed check and use the new result.
feat.archaeologists-luck.trigger: You fail a check against a trap, such as a [[skill.thievery|Thievery]] check to [[action.disable-a-device|Disable]] the trap or a Reflex save to avoid its effects.
feat.archer-dedication.name: Archer Dedication
feat.archer-dedication.text:
You have familiarity with all weapons in the bow and crossbow weapon groups. For the purposes of proficiency, treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

If you are at least an expert in the bow or crossbow you are using, you get the critical specialization effect of that weapon when you get a critical hit with it.
feat.archers-aim.name: Archer's Aim
feat.archers-aim.text: You slow down, focus, and take a careful shot. Make a ranged Strike with a weapon in the bow or crossbow weapon group. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack roll and ignore the target's [[condition.concealed|concealed]] condition. If the target is [[condition.hidden|hidden]], reduce the flat check from being hidden from 11 to 5.
feat.archwizards-might.name: Archwizard's Might
feat.archwizards-might.text: You have mastered the greatest secrets of arcane magic. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.
feat.armament-paragon.name: Armament Paragon
feat.armament-paragon.text: Add the following property runes to the list you can choose for your blessed armament: animated, greater fearsome, grievous, keen, and greater vitalizing. If you have the Radiant Armament feat, add greater astral and greater brilliant to the list as well. In addition, you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list as a single action that has the [[trait.concentrate|concentrate]] and [[trait.divine|divine]] traits. Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times.
feat.armor-assist.name: Armor Assist
feat.armor-assist.prereq.0: Trained in Warfare Lore or Trained in Athletics
feat.armor-assist.text: You are practiced in helping yourself and others don heavy gear. You can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check with a DC determined by the GM (usually DC 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor) to halve the time you take to don armor. You can halve an ally's time to don armor by working with them to don the armor and succeeding at an Athletics or Warfare Lore check against the same DC.
feat.armor-proficiency.name: Armor Proficiency
feat.armor-proficiency.text:
You become trained in light armor. If you already were trained in light armor, you gain training in medium armor. If you were trained in both, you become trained in heavy armor. If you are at least 13th level, you become an expert in this armor type.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you become trained in the next type of armor, as detailed above.
feat.armor-specialist.name: Armor Specialist
feat.armor-specialist.text: You have trained hard to optimize your armor's unique protective qualities to maximize the materials used in its creation. You gain the armor specialization effects for all armors you are proficient with.
feat.armored-rebuff.name: Armored Rebuff
feat.armored-rebuff.requirements: You are wearing medium armor or heavier.
feat.armored-rebuff.text: You rebuff puny attacks with your armor, knocking back your foe. Attempt an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.shove|Shove]] the triggering enemy, even if you don't have a hand free. If you succeed, you can't [[action.stride|Stride]] to follow the enemy, as you're knocking the enemy back with the rebounded attack, not by physically moving towards them.
feat.armored-rebuff.trigger: An adjacent enemy critically fails an attack roll to [[action.strike|Strike]] you with a melee weapon or unarmed attack.
feat.armored-stealth.name: Armored Stealth
feat.armored-stealth.text: You have learned techniques to adjust and modify your armor and movements to reduce the noise you make. When you wear non-[[trait.noisy|noisy]] armor with which you are trained, your penalty to Stealth checks is reduced by 1 (to a minimum penalty of 0). If you're a master in Stealth, reduce the penalty by 2, and if you're legendary, reduce the penalty by 3. If your armor has the noisy trait, instead of reducing the penalty to Stealth checks, you ignore the effects of the noisy trait, enabling you to remove the penalty with a sufficient Strength score as normal.
feat.ask-the-bones.name: Ask the Bones
feat.ask-the-bones.text: You keep the bone of an ancestor or a friend to call upon for advice. Attempt to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]]. If the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check.
feat.assassin-dedication.name: Assassin Dedication
feat.assassin-dedication.text:
You've trained to assassinate your foes, and you do so with tenacity and precision. You gain the Mark for Death activity.

** Mark for Death** {3a} ([[trait.concentrate|concentrate]]) **Requirements** The creature you intend to mark is [[condition.observed|observed]] by you; **Effect** You designate a single creature as your mark. Using Mark for Death while hidden or undetected doesn't make you observed. Mark for Death lasts until the mark dies or you use Mark for Death again. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek your mark, as well as to Deception checks to Feint against your mark. Your mark takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all Perception checks to Seek you.
