In addition, when attacking your mark, you have the [[class.rogue|sneak attack]] class feature, except it deals 1d4 precision damage and you don't increase the number of dice as you gain levels. At 6th level, the damage increases to 1d6. If you already have the sneak attack class feature, you instead deal an additional 1 precision damage with your sneak attacks made against your mark, increasing to 2 precision damage at 6th level.
feat.assassinate.name: Assassinate
feat.assassinate.requirements: You have designated a mark using Mark for Death and are completely [[condition.unnoticed|unnoticed]] by your mark.
feat.assassinate.text: You strike with one swift movement, trying to instantly slay your mark. Make a Strike against your mark. If you hit, your mark takes an additional 6d6 precision damage with a basic Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the mark critically fails, it dies unless its level is higher than yours. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is temporarily immune to your Assassinate for 1 day.
feat.assisting-shot.name: Assisting Shot
feat.assisting-shot.requirements: You are wielding a ranged weapon
feat.assisting-shot.text: Using your last shot to gauge your accuracy, you can fire off a quick shot to interfere with a foe in combat. Make a Strike with a ranged weapon. If the Strike hits, the next creature other than you to attack the same target before the start of your next turn gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their roll, or a +2 circumstance bonus if your Strike was a critical hit.
feat.assurance.name: Assurance
feat.assurance.prereq.0: trained in at least one skill
feat.assurance.text:
Even in the worst circumstances, you can perform basic tasks. Choose a skill you're trained in. You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different skill and gain the benefits for that skill.
feat.assured-identification.name: Assured Identification
feat.assured-identification.text: You rarely misidentify an item. When using Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion checks to [[action.identify-magic|Identify Magic]], if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. If you would misidentify a [[trait.cursed|cursed]] item because you roll a success but not a critical success, you simply can't identify it instead.
feat.assured-knowledge.name: Assured Knowledge
feat.assured-knowledge.text:
You can procure information with confidence. Whenever you [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] using any skill (including [[feat.bardic-lore|Bardic Lore]]), you can forgo rolling your check to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (don’t apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).

As long as you are an expert in a skill, you meet the prerequisites for the [[feat.automatic-knowledge|Automatic Knowledge]] skill feat for that skill, even if you don’t have the [[feat.assurance|Assurance]] feat for that skill.
feat.assured-ritualist.name: Assured Ritualist
feat.assured-ritualist.text: You can cover for a secondary caster's error. If you are the primary caster, after all the secondary checks are rolled, you can choose one check that was a failure or critical failure, and improve the result to one degree of success better than what the secondary caster rolled.
feat.athletic-might.name: Athletic Might
feat.athletic-might.text: Surviving in hostile terrain has given you a great talent for mobility. Whenever you roll a success on an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.climb|Climb]] or [[action.swim|Swim]], you get a critical success instead.
feat.athletic-strategist.name: Athletic Strategist
feat.athletic-strategist.text:
You know how to calculatedly manipulate joints and body weight. In addition to using an attack stratagem's roll substitution for a Strike, you can use it to modify a [[action.disarm|Disarm]], [[action.grapple|Grapple]], [[action.reposition|Reposition]], [[action.shove|Shove]], or [[action.trip|Trip]] attempt, substituting your [[action.devise-a-stratagem|Devise a Stratagem]] roll for the [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check. You must apply the substitution to the first eligible attack you make, whether it's a Strike or one of the Athletics actions.

You can also use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for the Athletics check when you substitute your Devise a Stratagem roll, unless you're using a weapon for the maneuver and the weapon doesn't fit the restrictions for using Intelligence with a stratagem.
feat.aura-of-courage.name: Aura of Courage
feat.aura-of-courage.text: You stand strong in the face of danger and inspire your allies to do the same. Whenever you become [[condition.frightened|frightened]], reduce the condition value by 1 (to a minimum of 0). At the end of your turn, each ally in your champion's aura reduces its frightened value by 1.
feat.aura-of-despair.name: Aura of Despair
feat.aura-of-despair.text: Your presence as an avatar of evil makes your foes more susceptible to terror and makes it almost impossible for them to shake off fear when you are near. Enemies in your champion's aura take a –1 circumstance penalty to saving throws against [[trait.fear|fear]]. In addition, an enemy that ends its turn in your champion's aura can't reduce the value of its [[condition.frightened|frightened]] condition below 1.
feat.aura-of-determination.name: Aura of Determination
feat.aura-of-determination.text: Your aura protects against powers that would twist the mind and body. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [[trait.mental|mental]], [[trait.morph|morph]], and [[trait.polymorph|polymorph]] effects.
feat.aura-of-faith.name: Aura of Faith
feat.aura-of-faith.text: You radiate an aura of belief that imbues your attacks and those of nearby allies with divine power. Each willing ally in your champion's aura adds the [[trait.holy|holy]] trait to their Strikes if you're holy or adds the [[trait.unholy|unholy]] trait to their Strikes if you're unholy.
feat.aura-of-life.name: Aura of Life
feat.aura-of-life.text: Your aura protects against the power of the Void. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain resistance 5 to void damage and a +1 status bonus to saves against [[trait.void|void]] effects.
feat.aura-of-righteousness.name: Aura of Righteousness
feat.aura-of-righteousness.text: Your righteous aura dampens evil's might and prevents the unholy from escaping you. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain resistance 5 to [[trait.unholy|unholy]] spells, unholy Strikes, and other unholy effects. If a [[trait.teleportation|teleportation]] spell or effect would teleport an unholy creature out of your champion's aura, your aura attempts to counteract it, using the spell rank and DC of your devotion spells.
feat.auspicious-mount.name: Auspicious Mount
feat.auspicious-mount.text:
Guided by your ongoing care, your steed has developed incredible intelligence and skill. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a specialized animal companion. You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization. A faithful steed with the auspice specialization gains the following benefits. 
- It gains the [[trait.celestial|celestial]], [[trait.fiend|fiend]], or [[trait.monitor|monitor]] trait—whichever best matches your deity's servitors, and its appearance shifts to look more like those servitors. It also gains the [[trait.holy|holy]] trait if it's a celestial or the [[trait.unholy|unholy]] trait if it's a fiend.
- Its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier by 1.
- Its proficiency rank in [[skill.religion|Religion]] increases to expert.
- It can speak the language associated with your deity's servitors (such as Empyrean for celestials, Chthonian for demons, or Requian for psychopomps).
- Its maximum Hit Points increase by 20, increasing to 25 at 18th level and 30 at 20th level. If the mount has the celestial trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to unholy. If it has the fiend trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to holy.
- It gains wings that grant it a fly Speed equal to its land Speed.
feat.automatic-knowledge.name: Automatic Knowledge
feat.automatic-knowledge.prereq.0: expert in a skill with the Recall Knowledge action
feat.automatic-knowledge.text:
You know basic facts off the top of your head. Choose a skill you’re an expert in that has the Recall Knowledge action and for which you have the Assurance feat. You can use the Recall Knowledge action with that skill as a free action once per round. If you do, you must use Assurance on the skill check.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a different skill each time. You can use Automatic Knowledge with any skills you have chosen, but you can still use Automatic Knowledge only once per round.
feat.avalanche-strike.name: Avalanche Strike
feat.avalanche-strike.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon in two hands.
feat.avalanche-strike.text: You attack all nearby adversaries. Make a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] with your two-handed weapon against each enemy within its melee reach. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don’t increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.
feat.avatars-audience.name: Avatar's Audience
feat.avatars-audience.text: Your extensive service affords you certain divine privileges. First, any creature you encounter knows instinctively that you speak for your deity. Second, if you conduct the commune ritual to contact your deity, you don’t have to pay any cost, and you automatically get a critical success. Third, once per day, you can cast interplanar teleport as a divine innate spell, but only to travel to the realm of your deity. When you cast it this way, its casting time is 1 minute, your religious symbol is a sufficient planar key for this spell, and you appear exactly where you want to be. If you’re in your deity’s realm due to this spell, you can return to the point you left when you cast it by spending a single action, which has the concentrate and divine traits.
feat.avatars-protection.name: Avatar's Protection
feat.avatars-protection.requirements: You have an avatar spell prepared
feat.avatars-protection.text: In moments of danger, you can call upon your god’s form in an instant. You cast avatar from your spell slots. The triggering critical hit is reduced to a normal hit, and its damage is applied after gaining the avatar spell’s temporary Hit Points.
feat.avatars-protection.trigger: You are critically hit by an enemy
feat.avenge-ally.name: Avenge Ally
feat.avenge-ally.requirements: You are within 30 feet of an ally with the dying condition
feat.avenge-ally.text: Though you know that you will eventually outlive your companions, seeing them at death's door brings clarity to your attacks. Make a [[action.strike|Strike]]. Roll twice on the attack roll and use the higher result.
feat.awesome-blow.name: Awesome Blow
feat.awesome-blow.text:
Your attacks are so powerful, they can flatten your opponents. When you use Knockback, you can attempt an Athletics check against your target's Fortitude DC.

**Critical Success** You gain the critical success effect of a [[action.shove|Shove]], then the critical success effect of a [[action.trip|Trip]] against the target.

**Success** You gain the success effect of a Shove, then the success effect of a Trip against the target.

**Failure** You gain the normal effect of Knockback.
feat.back-to-back.name: Back to Back
feat.back-to-back.text: You excel at watching your allies’ backs and helping them watch yours. Any ally adjacent to you can’t be [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] due to flanking unless you’re also flanked. Similarly, while you’re adjacent to at least one ally, you can’t be off-guard due to flanking unless at least one ally you’re adjacent to is flanked as well.
feat.backup-disguise.name: Backup Disguise
feat.backup-disguise.text: You have a specific disguise that you keep at the ready, worn underneath your outer garment. You can change into this disguise to [[action.impersonate|Impersonate]] as a 3-action activity. If you are a master in Deception, it is instead a 2-action activity, and if you are legendary in Deception, it is a single action. You can create a new backup disguise by spending the normal amount of time it takes you to Impersonate, but you can have only one backup disguise at a time. Having a backup disguise doesn't allow you to remove your armor or any other complex piece of clothing any more quickly, but once you have those off, the disguise is readily available. Because you have the backup disguise at the ready, it's possible that a thorough search might reveal some elements of the [[action.conceal-an-object|disguise]].
feat.barbarian-dedication.name: Barbarian Dedication
feat.barbarian-dedication.text: You become trained in Athletics; if you were already trained in [[skill.athletics|Athletics]], you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in barbarian class DC. You can use the Rage action. While raging, you take a –1 penalty to AC. Choose an instinct as you would if you were a barbarian. You have that instinct for all purposes, but you don’t gain any of the other abilities it grants. If that instinct has anathema, you’re bound by them.
feat.barbarian-resiliency.name: Barbarian Resiliency
feat.barbarian-resiliency.prereq.1: class granting no more Hit Points per level than 10 + your Constitution modifier
feat.barbarian-resiliency.text: You gain 3 additional Hit Points for each barbarian archetype class feat you have. As you continue selecting barbarian archetype class feats, you continue to gain additional Hit Points in this way.
feat.bard-dedication.name: Bard Dedication
feat.bard-dedication.text:
You cast spells like a bard and gain the [[action.cast-a-spell|Cast a Spell]] activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two common cantrips from the occult spell list or any other occult cantrips you’ve learned or discovered. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for bard archetype spells is Charisma, and they are occult bard spells. You become trained in Occultism and Performance; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

Choose a muse as you would if you were a bard. You can take that muse’s feats, but you don’t gain the starting feat, spell or any other abilities the choice of muse grants.
feat.bardic-lore.name: Bardic Lore
feat.bardic-lore.text: Your studies make you informed on every subject. You are trained in Bardic Lore, a special Lore skill that can be used only to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]], but on any topic. If you have legendary proficiency in [[skill.occultism|Occultism]], you gain expert proficiency in Bardic Lore, but you can’t increase your proficiency rank in Bardic Lore by any other means.
feat.bargain-hunter.name: Bargain Hunter
feat.bargain-hunter.text: You can [[action.earn-income|Earn Income]] using [[skill.diplomacy|Diplomacy]], spending your days hunting for bargains and reselling at a profit. You can also spend time specifically sniffing out a great bargain on an item; this works as if you were using Earn Income with Diplomacy, except instead of gaining money, you purchase the item at a discount equal to the money you would have gained, gaining the item for free if your earned income equals or exceeds its cost. Finally, if you select Bargain Hunter during character creation at 1st level, you start play with an additional 2 gp.
feat.bark-and-tendril.name: Bark and Tendril
feat.bark-and-tendril.text: You wield primal magic. You can cast [[spell.entangling-flora|entangling flora]] and [[spell.oaken-resilience|oaken resilience]] as 2nd-rank primal innate spells once per day each.
feat.barreling-charge.name: Barreling Charge
feat.barreling-charge.text: You rush forward, moving enemies aside to reach your foe. You [[action.stride|Stride]], attempting to move through your enemies’ spaces. Roll an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check and compare the result to the Fortitude DC of each creature whose space you attempt to move through during your Stride, moving through its space on a success but ending your movement before entering its space on a failure. You can then [[action.strike|Strike]], regardless of how your Stride ended. You can use Barreling Charge to [[action.burrow|Burrow]], [[action.climb|Climb]], [[action.fly|Fly]], or [[action.swim|Swim]] instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.
feat.bashing-charge.name: Bashing Charge
feat.bashing-charge.text: You smash, bust, and charge through solid obstacles without hesitation. Stride twice. Once during your movement, if your movement passes through or ends adjacent to a door, window, fence, wall, or similar obstacle, you can attempt an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.force-open|Force Open]] the obstacle with a +1 circumstance bonus to the roll; on a failure, your movement ends at that obstacle.
feat.basic-arcana.name: Basic Arcana
feat.basic-arcana.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level wizard feat of your choice.
feat.basic-bard-spellcasting.name: Basic Bard Spellcasting
feat.basic-bard-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits.. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the bard archetype, add a common occult spell of the appropriate rank, or another appropriate occult spell you learned or discovered, to your repertoire.
feat.basic-blood-potency.name: Basic Blood Potency
feat.basic-blood-potency.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level sorcerer feat.
feat.basic-bloodline-spell.name: Basic Bloodline Spell
feat.basic-bloodline-spell.text: You gain your bloodline’s initial bloodline spell. If you don’t already have one, you also gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can [[action.refocus|Refocus]] without any special effort.
feat.basic-cleric-spellcasting.name: Basic Cleric Spellcasting
feat.basic-cleric-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. You can prepare your deity’s spells in your spell slots of the appropriate rank from the cleric archetype.
feat.basic-concoction.name: Basic Concoction
feat.basic-concoction.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level alchemist feat.
feat.basic-deduction.name: Basic Deduction
feat.basic-deduction.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level investigator feat of your choice.
feat.basic-devotion.name: Basic Devotion
feat.basic-devotion.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level champion feat.
feat.basic-dogma.name: Basic Dogma
feat.basic-dogma.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level cleric feat.
feat.basic-druid-spellcasting.name: Basic Druid Spellcasting
feat.basic-druid-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits.
You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new level from this archetype, add a spell of the appropriate spell rank to your repertoire, either a common spell of your chosen tradition or another spell of that tradition you have learned or discovered.
feat.basic-flair.name: Basic Flair
feat.basic-flair.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level swashbuckler feat of your choice.
feat.basic-fury.name: Basic Fury
feat.basic-fury.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level barbarian feat.
feat.basic-hunters-trick.name: Basic Hunter's Trick
feat.basic-hunters-trick.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level ranger feat.
feat.basic-kata.name: Basic Kata
feat.basic-kata.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level monk feat.
feat.basic-lesson.name: Basic Lesson
feat.basic-lesson.text: Your patron grants you a special lesson, revealing a hidden facet of its nature. Choose a basic lesson from the list here. You gain its associated hex, and your familiar learns the associated spell.
feat.basic-maneuver.name: Basic Maneuver
feat.basic-maneuver.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level fighter feat.
feat.basic-muses-whispers.name: Basic Muse's Whispers
feat.basic-muses-whispers.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level bard feat.
feat.basic-mysteries.name: Basic Mysteries
feat.basic-mysteries.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level oracle feat of your choice.
feat.basic-oracle-spellcasting.name: Basic Oracle Spellcasting
feat.basic-oracle-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. When you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the oracle archetype, add a common divine spell or another divine spell you have learned or discovered (including the granted spells associated with your mystery) to your repertoire, of that spell rank.
feat.basic-scroll-cache.name: Basic Scroll Cache
feat.basic-scroll-cache.text:
You have a vast and overflowing collection of scroll scraps, riddled with errors and misspellings and leaking energy like a sieve. With enough care, you can coax these scroll scraps into functioning—briefly. Each day during your daily preparations, you can create a single temporary scroll containing a 1st-rank spell. The spell must be a common spell, a spell to which you have access, or a spell you are able to cast, and you must be trained in the skill corresponding to at least one of the spell's traditions. You can use [[action.learn-a-spell|Learn a Spell]] to add spells to those you can use with this feat, even if you aren't a spellcaster. This scroll is an unstable, temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. This temporary scroll can't be used to Learn the Spell. 
At 8th level, add a second temporary scroll containing a 2nd-rank spell.
feat.basic-sorcerer-spellcasting.name: Basic Sorcerer Spellcasting
feat.basic-sorcerer-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the sorcerer archetype, add a spell of the appropriate spell rank to your repertoire: a common spell of your bloodline’s tradition, one of your bloodline’s granted spells, or another spell you have learned or discovered.
feat.basic-trickery.name: Basic Trickery
feat.basic-trickery.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level rogue feat.
feat.basic-wilding.name: Basic Wilding
feat.basic-wilding.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level druid feat.
feat.basic-witch-spellcasting.name: Basic Witch Spellcasting
feat.basic-witch-spellcasting.text: You gain the spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the witch archetype, add two common spells of that rank to your familiar.
feat.basic-witchcraft.name: Basic Witchcraft
feat.basic-witchcraft.text: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level witch feat of your choice. You can select three familiar abilities for your familiar each day, instead of two.
feat.basic-wizard-spellcasting.name: Basic Wizard Spellcasting
feat.basic-wizard-spellcasting.text: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the wizard archetype, add two common spells of that rank to your spellbook.
feat.bastion-dedication.name: Bastion Dedication
feat.bastion-dedication.text: You are particularly skilled at using a shield to protect yourself in combat. You gain the [[feat.reactive-shield|Reactive Shield]] fighter feat.
feat.battle-cry.name: Battle Cry
feat.battle-cry.text: When you roll initiative, you can yell a mighty battle cry and Demoralize an observed foe as a free action. If you’re legendary in Intimidation, you can use a reaction to Demoralize your foe when you critically succeed at an attack roll.
feat.battle-medicine.name: Battle Medicine
feat.battle-medicine.requirements: You're holding or wearing a [[item.healers-toolkit|healer's toolkit]].
feat.battle-medicine.text: You can patch up wounds, even in combat. Attempt a Medicine check with the same DC as for [[action.treat-wounds|Treat Wounds]] and restore the corresponding amount of HP; this doesn’t remove the wounded condition. As with Treat Wounds, you can attempt checks against higher DCs if you have the minimum proficiency rank. The target is then immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day. This does not make them immune to, or otherwise count as, Treat Wounds.
feat.battle-planner.name: Battle Planner
feat.battle-planner.text: You are constantly drawing up plans and battle scenarios, assembling strategies and gathered intelligence for later use. When you scout an enemy's position or receive a detailed report from an ally who scouted the enemy's position, if you have a clear indication of the number, position, and identities of your potential foes, you can spend 1 minute to come up with a battle plan that takes such potential factors into account and reduces the role luck plays in the equation. Roll a Warfare Lore check. As long as the information was accurate and remains accurate when you roll initiative against those enemies, you can use the Warfare Lore result you previously rolled for your initiative roll; if you do, this is a [[trait.fortune|fortune]] effect.
feat.beast-trainer.name: Beast Trainer
feat.beast-trainer.text: You have an impressive innate ability to tame and command ferocious beasts. You become trained in the [[skill.nature|Nature]] skill and gain your choice of the [[feat.pet|Pet]] general feat or the [[feat.train-animal|Train Animal]] skill feat.
feat.beastmaster-bond.name: Beastmaster Bond
feat.beastmaster-bond.text: You can communicate telepathically with your animal companions within 100 feet. If you’re legendary in [[skill.nature|Nature]], you can communicate telepathically with your animal companions anywhere on the planet.
feat.beastmaster-dedication.name: Beastmaster Dedication
feat.beastmaster-dedication.text:
You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you and obeys your commands. Contrary to the usual rules for animal companions, this feat can grant you a second animal companion. If you ever have more than one animal companion, you gain the Call Companion action.

Certain beastmaster feats give you focus spells. When you gain your first beastmaster focus spell, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for beastmaster archetype spells is Charisma, and they are primal spells. You can [[action.refocus|Refocus]] by feeding, playing with, or otherwise tending to an animal companion.

**Beastmaster Animal Companions**

If you're playing a beastmaster, you determine the statistics and abilities of your animal companions. As a beastmaster, it's possible for you to have more than one animal companion at one time—up to four companions—but only one of those companions, your “active companion,” follows you during exploration and in encounters; the rest are nearby, usually foraging or hunting for food. As soon as you gain a second animal companion from the Beastmaster archetype, you also gain Call Companion to switch your active companion. These rules apply to all your companions, regardless of whether you got the animal companion from the beastmaster archetype or from another source.
feat.beastmasters-call.name: Beastmaster's Call
feat.beastmasters-call.text: You quickly call in a primal projection of a non-active companion to provide the companion’s support benefit. The projection arrives in an unoccupied square of your choice within 30 feet of you, grants you its support benefit, and then disappears at the start of your next turn. The projection has the same AC and saving throw modifiers as the real companion, and if it would take any damage before your next turn, it disappears, and the support benefit ends immediately.
feat.beastmasters-trance.name: Beastmaster's Trance
feat.beastmasters-trance.text: You can enter a trance that allows you to briefly inhabit the body of one of your animal companions and share its senses. You gain the focus spell [[spell.beastmaster-trance|_beastmaster trance_]].
feat.benefactors-majesty.name: Benefactor's Majesty
feat.benefactors-majesty.text: You tap into the grandeur of your warren's benefactor. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level, which last for 1 minute. In addition, you can immediately attempt a flat check to remove each type of [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent damage]] you have. Finally, until the start of your next turn, any creature targeting you with a harmful attack, spell, or ability much first succeed at a DC 11 flat check or the action is disrupted as the creature avoids setting eyes upon your majesty.
feat.bespell-strikes.name: Bespell Strikes
feat.bespell-strikes.requirements: Your most recent action was to cast a non-cantrip spell
feat.bespell-strikes.text:
You siphon spell energy into one weapon you’re wielding, or into one of your unarmed attacks, such as a fist. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or unarmed attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the associated trait (see below) if it didn’t have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).

**Oracle**: Your strike gains the [[trait.divine|divine]] trait.

**Sorcerer:** Your strike gains the trait of your bloodline’s magical tradition.

**Wizard**: Your strike gains the [[trait.arcane|arcane]] trait.
feat.bestial-manifestation.name: Bestial Manifestation
feat.bestial-manifestation.text:
Part of your body has an animalistic influence from a planar creature. Your hands end in claws, you have hooves instead of feet, sharp teeth fill your mouth, or a tail extends from your spine. You gain your choice of one of the following unarmed attacks. The attack is in the brawling group and has the listed damage die and traits.

- **Claw** 1d4 slashing ([[trait.agile|agile]], [[trait.finesse|finesse]], [[trait.unarmed|unarmed]], [[trait.versatile|versatile]] piercing)
- **Hoof** 1d6 bludgeoning (finesse, unarmed)
- **Jaws** 1d6 piercing (finesse, unarmed)
- **Tail** 1d4 bludgeoning (agile, finesse, unarmed)

**Special** You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can’t retrain into or out of this feat, nor can you change the type of attack you gained.
feat.between-the-scales.name: Between the Scales
feat.between-the-scales.text: You've learned to take advantage of slips in your foes' defenses. When you Strike an [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] creature using a melee weapon or unarmed attack that has the [[trait.agile|agile]] and [[trait.finesse|finesse]] traits, it gains the [[trait.backstabber|backstabber]] trait.
feat.big-mouth.name: Big Mouth
feat.big-mouth.text: Instead of storing up to four items of Light Bulk in your cheek pouches, you can store up to 1 Bulk worth of items. The maximum size of a given item is unchanged.
feat.biographical-eye.name: Biographical Eye
feat.biographical-eye.text:
In even a brief conversation or social interaction, you pick up on subtle social and visual cues to learn a great deal about a person's origin and history. You might notice bits of green under the person's fingernails and determine they're an herbalist, spy a pin indicating their membership in a secret society, or something similar. You pick up on only details that have to do with their societal role, so you might learn the city district where a vampire lives, but wouldn't learn any of their weaknesses, nor necessarily even that they are a vampire. 
Spend 1 minute in the presence of someone you haven't met before, or haven't met since you first gained Biographical Eye, then attempt a DC 30 Society check. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the check if you engaged the person in conversation during this time. If the person is deliberately trying to conceal their nature or present a false identity, you learn about their false biography rather than their true one unless the result of your Society check exceeds their Will DC.

**Critical Success** You learn the creature's profession, their specialty within that profession, and a major accomplishment or controversy from their career. You also learn the nation and settlement where they live, as well as the district in a city large enough to have districts. In addition, you learn the nation or settlement where they spent their formative years.

**Success** You learn the creature's profession and specialty within that profession. You learn the nation or settlement where they normally live.

**Failure** You learn the creature's profession and the region of the world they hail from, but no more.

**Critical Failure** You learn a piece of erroneous information about the creature.
feat.bizarre-magic.name: Bizarre Magic
feat.bizarre-magic.text: You can draw upon strange variations in your spellcasting, whether or not you can cast occult spells. The DCs to Recognize Spells you cast and Identify Magic you use increase by 5.
feat.black-cat-curse.name: Black Cat Curse
feat.black-cat-curse.text: You hiss a spiteful curse. The target rerolls the triggering saving throw and use the worse result.
feat.black-cat-curse.trigger: A creature within 30 feet you can see would succeed at a save.
feat.blade-brake.name: Blade Brake
feat.blade-brake.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon and are within reach of a hard surface
feat.blade-brake.text: You plow your weapon into a floor, wall, or another sturdy surface, anchoring yourself in place. If you would be moved 20 feet or more, you are moved only 5 feet. Otherwise, you don’t move at all.
feat.blade-brake.trigger: You would be moved by a forced movement effect
feat.blank-slate.name: Blank Slate
feat.blank-slate.text: Your deceptions confound even the most powerful magic that could spy on you. Detection, revelation, and scrying effects pass right over you, your possessions, and your auras, detecting nothing unless the detecting effect has a counteract rank of 10 or higher. For example, detect magic would still detect other magic in the area but not any magic on you, truesight wouldn’t reveal you, locate or scrying wouldn’t find you, and so on.
feat.blaze-of-revelation.name: Blaze of Revelation
feat.blaze-of-revelation.text:
Your mind and body can, for a short time and with great peril, surpass the final limits of your curse. For 1 minute, you shed torrential flames, become surrounded by spirits, or otherwise overflow with [[trait.divine|divine]] power in a way that suits your mystery. On each of your turns during that time, you can cast one revelation spell without spending Focus Points. 
At the end of the minute, the durations of any revelation spells you cast during that time end, and you must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save.

**Critical Success** You aren’t otherwise affected.

**Success** You are [[condition.drained|drained]] 2 and can't reduce or remove this condition until your next preparations.

**Failure** You are drained 4 and can't reduce or remove this condition until your next preparations.

**Critical Failure** You die.
feat.bleed-out.name: Bleed Out
feat.bleed-out.requirements: Your most recent action was to [[action.cast-a-spell|cast]] a non-cantrip spell that granted you a blood magic effect.
feat.bleed-out.text: You channel the residual energy from the last spell you cast into a ranged bloodletting. Make a ranged spell [[trait.attack|attack]] roll against the AC of a target within 60 feet. This attack deals [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]] equal to the rank of the spell you just cast.
feat.bleeding-finisher.name: Bleeding Finisher
feat.bleeding-finisher.text: Your blow inflicts profuse bleeding. Make a slashing or piercing Strike. If you hit, the target also takes [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]] equal to your precise strike finisher damage.
feat.blessed-blood-nephilim.name: Blessed Blood
feat.blessed-blood-nephilim.text: Your spilled blood is sanctified, with effects similar to those of holy water. Whenever a [[trait.fiend|fiend]], [[trait.undead|undead]], or creature with a weakness to holy drinks your blood or deals piercing or slashing damage to you with jaws, fangs, or a similar attack, that creature takes 1d6 spirit damage with the [[trait.holy|holy]] trait. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to [[skill.crafting|Crafting]] checks to [[action.craft|Craft]] holy water using your blood as one of the ingredients.
feat.blessed-counterstrike.name: Blessed Counterstrike
feat.blessed-counterstrike.prereq.0: champion’s reaction that grants an ally resistance to an enemy’s damage (including the grandeur, justice, liberation, and redemption causes)
feat.blessed-counterstrike.requirements: An enemy triggered your champion’s reaction since the end of your last turn.
feat.blessed-counterstrike.text: You call upon divine power and make a weapon or unarmed Strike against the enemy who triggered your champion's reaction. The Strike deals one extra weapon damage die. If this Strike hits, until the start of your next turn, the target gains weakness equal to half your level to all Strikes made by you and your allies.
feat.blessed-denial.name: Blessed Denial
feat.blessed-denial.text: You exude peace and protection, lessening a harmful condition as it falls upon an ally. Reduce the value of the condition your ally would take by 1 (to a minimum of 0). If the ally has more than one eligible condition at the same time, choose one to reduce.
feat.blessed-denial.trigger: An ally within 30 feet would become [[condition.frightened|frightened]], [[condition.drained|drained]], [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled]], [[condition.sickened|sickened]], or [[condition.stupefied|stupefied]].
feat.blessed-one-dedication.name: Blessed One Dedication
feat.blessed-one-dedication.text: You are touched by a deity and gifted with the ability to alleviate the suffering of others. You gain the [[spell.lay-on-hands|_lay on hands_]] devotion spell. You can [[action.refocus|Refocus]] by meditating, whether you reflect on the deity granting the blessing or not, allowing your blessing to refill your focus pool. Your devotion spells from the blessed one archetype are divine spells. You become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. Your spellcasting attribute is Charisma.
feat.blessed-sacrifice.name: Blessed Sacrifice
feat.blessed-sacrifice.text: You gain the [[spell.protectors-sacrifice|_protector’s sacrifice_]] domain spell as a devotion spell.
feat.blessed-spell.name: Blessed Spell
feat.blessed-spell.prereq.2: ability to cast spells from spell slots
feat.blessed-spell.text: When you focus your magic on an ally, you can remove harmful conditions. If your next action is to [[action.cast-a-spell|Cast a Spell]] from a spell slot, and that spell targets only a single ally, you can also attempt to remove a harmful condition from that ally. The condition must be one that could be removed by your [[feat.mercy|Mercy]] feat, including those granted by later feats such as [[feat.greater-mercy|Greater Mercy]]. Attempt a counteract check based on the spell’s DC and rank. This effect is in addition to the normal effects of your spell.
feat.blind-fight.name: Blind-Fight
feat.blind-fight.text:
Your battle instincts make you more aware of concealed and invisible opponents. You don’t need to succeed at a flat check to target concealed creatures. You’re not off-guard to creatures that are hidden from you (unless you’re off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful DC 5 flat check to target a hidden creature.

While you’re adjacent to an undetected creature of your level or lower, it is instead only hidden from you
feat.blood-ascendancy.name: Blood Ascendancy
feat.blood-ascendancy.text: When you would benefit from a blood magic effect through Blood Rising, you can choose to benefit from two different blood magic effects you know. The effects follow the same rules as given in Blood Rising, and each effect can have a different target.
feat.blood-rising.name: Blood Rising
feat.blood-rising.text:
The magic in your blood surges in response to your foe's spell. You generate a blood magic effect you know, even if you are already under the effects of blood magic. The target must be either you or the creature that triggered Blood Rising. If the blood magic effect grants you a bonus to AC or the appropriate saving throw, that bonus applies against the triggering spell. If the effect has a duration, it instead lasts until the beginning of your next turn.

**Special** This feat has the traitcorresponding to the tradition of your bloodline.
feat.blood-rising.trigger: A creature targets you with a spell of the same tradition as your bloodline.
feat.blood-sovereignty.name: Blood Sovereignty
feat.blood-sovereignty.text: You wield blood magic masterfully. When you would benefit from a blood magic effect, you can choose to lose Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank as the energy of your blood is drawn out. This takes no extra action, and you benefit from two different blood magic effects you know as a result. The two effects can have different targets.
feat.bloodletting-fangs.name: Bloodletting Fangs
feat.bloodletting-fangs.text: You emulate your vampiric parent's techniques for drawing blood from a victim. Your fangs Strikes deal an additional 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]] on a critical hit.
feat.bloodline-breadth.name: Bloodline Breadth
feat.bloodline-breadth.text: Your repertoire expands, and you can cast more spells of your bloodline’s tradition each day. Increase the number of spells in your repertoire and number of spell slots you gain from sorcerer archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest sorcerer spell slots.
feat.bloodline-conduit.name: Bloodline Conduit
feat.bloodline-conduit.text: Your inborn magical nature lets you redirect ambient energies to fuel your spells. If your next action is to [[action.cast-a-spell|Cast a Spell]] of 5th rank or lower that has no duration, you don't expend the spell's slot when you cast it.
feat.bloodline-focus.name: Bloodline Focus
feat.bloodline-focus.text: By listening to the beating of your heart, your focus recovers faster. Whenever you [[action.refocus|Refocus]], completely refill your focus pool.
feat.bloodline-mutation.name: Bloodline Mutation
feat.bloodline-mutation.prereq.0: a bloodline based on a specific type of creature
feat.bloodline-mutation.text:
You permanently mutate to become more like the creatures of your bloodline. You gain the appropriate trait or traits for those types of creatures ([[trait.aberration|aberration]] for aberrant, angel and [[trait.celestial|celestial]] for angelic, demon and [[trait.fiend|fiend]] for demonic, and so on). You gain low-light vision or darkvision, if one is appropriate for creatures with those traits. Choose one of the following. 
- If the creatures associated with your bloodline have the ability to [[action.fly|fly]], you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed.
- If the creatures associated with your bloodline are [[trait.aquatic|aquatic]] or [[trait.amphibious|amphibious]], you become amphibious, able to breathe water and air equally well, and you gain a [[action.swim|swim]] Speed equal to your land Speed.
- If creatures associated with your bloodline have a resistance or immunity to [[trait.acid|acid]], [[trait.cold|cold]], [[trait.electricity|electricity]], [[trait.fire|fire]], [[trait.void|void]], or [[trait.sonic|sonic]],choose an energy type your bloodline is immune or resistant to and gain resistance 20 against that energy type.
feat.bloodline-perfection.name: Bloodline Perfection
feat.bloodline-perfection.text: You command the ultimate powers of your bloodline and tradition. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.
feat.bloodline-resistance.name: Bloodline Resistance
feat.bloodline-resistance.text: Your magical blood makes you more resistant to magic. You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against spells and [[trait.magical|magical]] effects.
feat.bloody-blows.name: Bloody Blows
feat.bloody-blows.text: Your lethal unarmed attacks leave bloody gouges or cause severe internal bleeding. When you critically hit with a [[action.strike|Strike]] using an unarmed attack that isn’t [[trait.nonlethal|nonlethal]], the target takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage. This can be because you’re taking the penalty to use a fist for a lethal attack or because you have an unarmed attack without the nonlethal trait due to Tusks or a similar ability.
feat.bloody-debilitation.name: Bloody Debilitation
feat.bloody-debilitation.text:
Your attacks slice arteries and veins. Add the following debilitation to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

- **Debilitation** The target takes 3d6 persistent bleed damage.
feat.blowgun-poisoner.name: Blowgun Poisoner
feat.blowgun-poisoner.text:
You can capably deliver toxins with a [[item.blowgun|blowgun]]. Your blowgun [[action.strike|Strikes]] can apply [[trait.injury|injury]] [[trait.poison|poisons]] even if they deal no damage due to a creature's resistance. If you critically succeed at a blowgun Strike using a poisoned dart, the target's initial save against the poison is one degree of success worse than the creature rolls; this is a [[trait.misfortune|misfortune]] effect.

In addition, if you make a blowgun Strike while [[condition.hidden|hidden]] or [[condition.undetected|undetected]], you don't automatically become [[condition.observed|observed]]. Instead, immediately attempt a [[skill.stealth|Stealth]] check against the Perception DC of the target. If you succeed, you don't become observed, and are hidden (if you were undetected, you still become hidden rather than remaining undetected).
feat.bon-mot.name: Bon Mot
feat.bon-mot.text:
You launch an insightful quip at a foe, distracting them. Choose a foe within 30 feet and roll a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC.

**Critical Success** The target is distracted and takes a –3 status penalty to Perception and Will saves for 1 minute. The target can end the effect early with a retort to your Bon Mot. This can either be a single action that has the [[trait.concentrate|concentrate]] trait or an appropriate skill action to frame their retort. The GM determines which skill actions qualify, though they must take at least 1 action. Typically, the retort needs to use a linguistic Charisma-based skill action.

**Success** As critical success, but the penalty is –2.

**Critical Failure** Your quip is atrocious. You take the same penalty an enemy would take had you succeeded. This ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed.
feat.bond-conservation.name: Bond Conservation
feat.bond-conservation.requirements: The last action you used was to Cast a Spell enabled by Drain Bonded Item
feat.bond-conservation.text: By efficiently and carefully manipulating the arcane energies unleashed by your bonded item, you can conserve just enough power to cast another spell, though this second spell is slightly weaker. You gain an extra use of Drain Bonded Item. You can use it to cast a spell 2 or more ranks lower than the previous spell, and must use it before the end of your next turn or you lose it.
feat.bonded-animal.name: Bonded Animal
feat.bonded-animal.text:
You forge strong connections with animals. You can spend 7 days of downtime regularly interacting with a normal animal (not a companion or other special animal) that is friendly or helpful to you. After this duration, attempt a [[skill.nature|Nature]] check against the animal's Will DC. If successful, you bond with the animal. The animal is permanently bonded to you until you form a bond with a different animal or do something egregious to break your bond.

A helpful animal is easier to [[action.command-an-animal|direct]]. If your bonded animal is level –1, it gains the [[trait.minion|minion]] trait, allowing you to command it more efficiently. The maximum level of creature that can be your minion increases to 3 if you're a master in Nature and to 11 if you're legendary.

**Special** You can’t have both a bonded animal and an animal companion (though you can have both a bonded animal and a pet or familiar).
feat.bonded-focus.name: Bonded Focus
feat.bonded-focus.text: Your connection to your bonded item increases your focus pool. Whenever you Refocus while your bonded item is in your possession, you completely refill your focus pool.
feat.bone-investiture.name: Bone Investiture
feat.bone-investiture.text: You encase yourself in spiritual dinosaur bones to become a Huge dinosaur. You can cast [[spell.dinosaur-form|_dinosaur form_]] on yourself as a 5th-rank innate spell once per day.
feat.bone-magic.name: Bone Magic
feat.bone-magic.text:
Your connection to your iruxi ancestors manifests as a simple primal spell that you cast using a fragment of an ancestor's bones. Choose one cantrip from either the occult spell list or the primal spell list. You can cast this cantrip as an innate spell at will, and it's heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.

**Special** Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult; this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite.
feat.bonekeepers-bane.name: Bonekeeper's Bane
feat.bonekeepers-bane.text: Whenever an enemy starts its turn adjacent to you, it must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is highest. On a failure, the enemy takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls and skill checks for as long as it remains adjacent to you. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is then temporarily immune to bonekeeper's bane for 24 hours.
feat.boulder-roll.name: Boulder Roll
feat.boulder-roll.text:
Your dwarven build allows you to push foes around, just like a mighty boulder tumbles through a subterranean cavern. Take a [[action.step|Step]] into the square of a foe that is your size or smaller, and the foe must move into the empty space directly behind it. The foe must move even if doing so places it in harm's way. The foe can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] DC to block your Step. If the foe attempts this saving throw, it takes bludgeoning damage equal to your level plus your Strength modifier unless it critically succeeds.

If the foe can't move into an empty space (if it is surrounded by solid objects or other creatures, for example), your Boulder Roll has no effect.
feat.bounce-back.name: Bounce Back
feat.bounce-back.text: You recover from near-death experiences with astounding resilience. Don’t increase the value of your [[condition.wounded|wounded]] condition due to losing the [[condition.dying|dying]] condition.
feat.boundless-reprisals.name: Boundless Reprisals
feat.boundless-reprisals.text: With a sixth sense for the flow of combat, you can quickly react to any situation as required. At the start of each enemy’s turn, you gain a reaction you can use only during that turn for any reaction from a class feat or class feature from the class that granted you this feat.
feat.bounty-hunter-dedication.name: Bounty Hunter Dedication
feat.bounty-hunter-dedication.text:
When focused on finding your quarry, you’re relentless. You gain the [[action.hunt-prey|Hunt Prey]] action. You can use Hunt Prey to designate a creature that you’ve observed, heard about, or learned about through some other means, such as a bounty board or wanted poster. In addition to the other benefits of Hunt Prey, you can designate a target as your prey while Gathering Information about them, in addition to designating them as your prey when Tracking them as normal. If you have already identified your target and selected them as your prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Gather Information about them.

If you already have Hunt Prey, you gain the [[feat.monster-hunter|Monster Hunter]] feat in addition to the other benefits of this feat.
feat.brandishing-draw.name: Brandishing Draw
feat.brandishing-draw.text: You draw and attack with the same motion. You Interact to draw a weapon, then either Strike or use a one-action [[trait.finisher|finisher]]. You must still meet any other requirements to use a finisher, and any Strike you make must be made with the weapon you drew.
feat.break-curse.name: Break Curse
feat.break-curse.text: You spend 8 hours praying or performing occult rites over the target, weakening a curse's power over them. Attempt to counteract the curse, using Occultism or Religion for your counteract check and half your level rounded up for the counteract rank. Break Curse only takes 10 minutes of prayer and rites if you are legendary in Occultism or Religion.
feat.breath-control.name: Breath Control
feat.breath-control.text: You can breathe even in hazardous or sparse air. You can hold your breath for 25 times as long as usual before suffocating. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against inhaled threats, such as inhaled poisons, and if you roll a success on such a saving throw, you get a critical success instead.
feat.breath-like-honey.name: Breath Like Honey
feat.breath-like-honey.text: You smell of honey and savory things. Your circumstance bonus to checks to [[action.make-an-impression|Make an Impression]] if the target can smell your breath increases to +2. In addition, you can cast [[spell.enthrall|_enthrall_]] as a 3rd-rank occult innate spell once per day, except the spell has a range of 30 feet and the [[trait.olfactory|olfactory]] trait instead of the [[trait.auditory|auditory]] trait. Targets don't gain any circumstance bonus for disagreeing with you.
feat.breath-of-the-dragon.name: Breath of the Dragon
feat.breath-of-the-dragon.text:
Tapping into the physiology of your draconic ancestor, you can exhale a torrent of energy in a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line, dealing 1d4 damage. Each creature in the area must attempt a basic saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4. The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar (see above). This ability has the trait associated with the type of damage it deals.
feat.briar-battler.name: Briar Battler
feat.briar-battler.text: When you're in difficult terrain from an environmental feature, you can [[action.take-cover|Take Cover]], even if the feature wouldn't ordinarily be large enough for you to Take Cover.
feat.brilliant-flash.name: Brilliant Flash
feat.brilliant-flash.text: Your light cleanses souls of fear. When you use [[action.flash-of-grandeur|Flash of Grandeur]], the attacker is also [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] for 1 round.
feat.brine-may.name: Brine May
feat.brine-may.text: Your mother was a [[creature.sea-hag|sea hag]], granting you one sea-green or blue eye. You find comfort both in the sea and on the shore. Whenever you roll a success on an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.swim|Swim]], you get a critical success instead. If you end your turn in water without having succeeded at a Swim action that round, you don’t sink (but you might still be moved by the current).
feat.brutal-beating.name: Brutal Beating
feat.brutal-beating.text: Your critical hits shakes your foes’ confidence. Whenever your Strike is a critical hit and deals damage, the target is frightened 1.
feat.brutal-bully.name: Brutal Bully
feat.brutal-bully.text: You push your foes around and leave bruises. While raging, when you successfully [[action.disarm|Disarm]], [[action.grapple|Grapple]], [[action.reposition|Reposition]], [[action.shove|Shove]], or [[action.trip|Trip]] an enemy, you deal that enemy bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier; add this to the damage from a critical success to Trip.
feat.brutal-critical.name: Brutal Critical
feat.brutal-critical.text: Your critical hits are particularly devastating. On a critical hit with a melee Strike, add one extra damage die. This is in addition to any extra dice you gain if the weapon is [[trait.deadly|deadly]] or [[trait.fatal|fatal]]. The target also takes [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]] equal to two damage dice.
feat.brutal-finish.name: Brutal Finish
feat.brutal-finish.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon in two hands
feat.brutal-finish.text:
Your final blow can make an impact even if it rebounds off a foe’s defenses. Make a Strike with a melee weapon you’re wielding in two hands. After the Strike, your turn ends. The Strike deals one additional weapon damage die, or two additional weapon damage dice if you’re at least 18th level. The Strike also gains the following failure effect.

**Failure** You deal damage equal to one weapon damage die of the required weapon. Increase this to two dice if you’re at least 18th level.
feat.brutish-shove.name: Brutish Shove
feat.brutish-shove.requirements: You are wielding a two-handed melee weapon
feat.brutish-shove.text:
Using the momentum of your last attack to throw your weight into another, you make your opponent stumble back. Make a Strike with a two-handed melee weapon. If you hit a target that is your size or smaller, that creature is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] until the end of your current turn, and you can automatically [[action.shove|Shove ]]it, with the same benefits as the Shove action (including the critical success effect, if your Strike was a critical hit). If you move to follow the target, your movement doesn't trigger reactions. This Strike has the following failure effect.

**Failure** The target becomes off-guard until the end of your current turn.
feat.buckler-dance.name: Buckler Dance
feat.buckler-dance.text: You spin your buckler defensively toward every attack. You constantly have your buckler raised as if you'd used [[action.raise-a-shield|Raise a Shield]], as long as you meet that action's requirements.
feat.bullseye.name: Bullseye
feat.bullseye.text: You carefully take aim to avoid your foe’s concealment and cover. On your next Strike with a thrown weapon before the end of your turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll and ignore your target’s concealed condition, as well as the target’s lesser cover or standard cover; if the target had greater cover, they instead have only standard cover against the Strike.
feat.burn-it.name: Burn It!
feat.burn-it.text: Fire fascinates you. Your spells and alchemical items that deal fire damage gain a status bonus to damage equal to half the spell's rank or one-quarter the item's level (minimum bonus +1). You also gain a +1 status bonus to any persistent fire damage you deal.
feat.cackle.name: Cackle
feat.cackle.text: Your patron’s power fills you with confidence, letting you sustain a magical working even as a quick burst of laughter leaves your lips. You learn the [[spell.cackle|_cackle_]] hex.
feat.cadence-call.name: Cadence Call
feat.cadence-call.text: You call out a quick cadence, guiding your allies into a more efficient rhythm. Each willing ally in your marshal’s aura is [[condition.quickened|quickened]] until the end of their next turn, and they can use the extra action only to [[action.stride|Stride]]. If an ally uses this extra action, at the end of its turn that ally becomes [[condition.slowed|slowed]] 1 until the end of its following turn.
feat.call-and-response.name: Call and Response
feat.call-and-response.text: Your composition takes the form of a call-and-response chant that lets your allies continue the effect without you. If your next action is to cast a composition cantrip with a duration of 1 round, it becomes a call. While the spell is active, one ally of your choice affected by the spell can respond to your call as a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits to extend the spell’s duration by 1 round. Only one ally can respond to a given call, and responding to the ally’s response has no additional effect
feat.call-of-the-dead-realm.name: Call of the Dead Realm
feat.call-of-the-dead-realm.text: You have a powerful connection to the realm of the dead and its courts, granting you the ability to travel to and from the realm of the dead. You can cast [[spell.interplanar-teleport|_interplanar teleport_]] as a divine innate spell twice per week. This can be used only to travel to the realm of the dead or from the realm of the dead to the Universe. Due to your unique connection to the realm of the dead, your body serves as the locus, and you don't require a planar key.
feat.call-of-the-green-man.name: Call of the Green Man
feat.call-of-the-green-man.text: You can call forth nearby nature spirits to augment your body. Once per day, you can cast [[spell.plant-form|plant form]] as a 5th-rank primal innate spell. When you reach 17th level, you can heighten the spell to 6th rank when you cast it.
feat.call-of-the-wild.name: Call of the Wild
feat.call-of-the-wild.text: You call upon the creatures of nature to come to your aid. You can spend 10 minutes in concert with nature to replace a spell you’ve prepared in one of your druid spell slots with a summon animal or summon plant or fungus spell of the same rank.
feat.call-the-swarm.name: Call the Swarm
feat.call-the-swarm.text: You give a shrill whistle and point, and a massive swarm of rats pours forth from the surrounding terrain to fill a 30-foot burst within 120 feet. The rats scurry over the ground and climb up walls and surfaces, biting and clawing as they deal 6d8 piercing damage to all enemies in the area. The rats continue to swarm in the area for the next minute, dealing 3d8 piercing damage to any enemy that ends its turn in the area and transforming the area into difficult terrain (though the rats allow you and your allies to pass normally). You can Dismiss the effect.
feat.call-wizardly-tools.name: Call Wizardly Tools
feat.call-wizardly-tools.text: You’re mystically connected to your wizardly tools, ensuring you can always find them when you’ve misplaced them. You teleport your bonded item or spellbook to you. It arrives in your hand if you have a free hand or at your feet if you don’t. The item must be within 1 mile and have 1 Bulk or less.
feat.call-your-shot.name: Call Your Shot
feat.call-your-shot.text:
When you successfully Play to the Crowd, add the following to the list of benefits you can choose from: 
- A creature you can see within 30 feet becomes [[condition.frightened|frightened 2]]. This effect has the [[trait.emotion|emotion]], [[trait.fear|fear]], [[trait.mental|mental]], and [[trait.visual|visual]] traits.
feat.called.name: Called
feat.called.text: You’ve heard the Call, and by resisting it, you’ve developed a bulwark against effects that target your mind. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saving throws against [[trait.mental|mental]] effects. If you roll a success on your saving throw against a mental effect that would make you [[condition.controlled|controlled]], you get a critical success instead.
feat.callow-may.name: Callow May
feat.callow-may.text: You are among the most common of changelings—those born to sweet hags—and a vibrant green eye signifies that parentage. Your mother’s manipulative nature and versatile voice gives you an edge when deceiving others. You gain the [[feat.charming-liar|Charming Liar]] skill feat. If you roll [[skill.deception|Deception]] for initiative, foes in that combat encounter that haven’t acted yet are [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] against you.
feat.camouflage.name: Camouflage
feat.camouflage.text: You alter your appearance to blend in to the wilderness. In natural terrain, you can Hide and Sneak even without cover or being concealed.
feat.canny-acumen.name: Canny Acumen
feat.canny-acumen.text: Your avoidance or observation is beyond the ken of most in your profession. Choose Fortitude saves, Reflex saves, Will saves, or Perception. You become an expert in your choice. At 17th level, you become a master in your choice.
feat.cant-fall-here.name: Can't Fall Here
feat.cant-fall-here.text: You physically help an ally remain standing and encourage them to push through their pain against dire odds. Your ally doesn't fall [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]] and remains at 1 Hit Point. The ally also gains a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute. Fighting onward with such an injury isn't without consequence; your ally's [[condition.wounded|wounded]] condition increases by 1.
feat.cant-fall-here.trigger: An adjacent and willing ally would be reduced to 0 HP but not killed.
feat.cantorian-reinforcement.name: Cantorian Reinforcement
feat.cantorian-reinforcement.text: The life energy that helped create the first hobgoblins is particularly potent in you, protecting you from ongoing maladies. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a [[trait.disease|disease]] or [[trait.poison|poison]], you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the [[class.fighter|battle hardened fighter class feature]]), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.
feat.cantorian-rejuvenation.name: Cantorian Rejuvenation
feat.cantorian-rejuvenation.text: The life-giving energy that flows in your blood revitalizes you. You recover 4d6 Hit Points and gain 10 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute. At 15th level, you instead recover 6d6 HP and gain 15 temporary HP.
feat.cantorian-restoration.name: Cantorian Restoration
feat.cantorian-restoration.text: The energy that flows in your blood can save a life in the direst of times. You prevent the creature from dying and restore 6d8 + your Constitution modifier Hit Points to it. You can't use Cantorian Restoration if the triggering effect was a [[trait.death|death]] effect or an effect that leaves no remains, such as [[spell.disintegrate|_disintegrate_]].
feat.cantorian-restoration.trigger: A living creature within 60 feet would die.
feat.cantrip-expansion.name: Cantrip Expansion
feat.cantrip-expansion.text:
Study broadens your range of simple spells.

**Prepared Caster (Cleric, Wizard, etc.)**: You can prepare two additional cantrips each day.
**Spontaneous Caster (Bard, Sorcerer, etc.)**: Add two additional cantrips from your spell list to your repertoire.
feat.caravan-leader.name: Caravan Leader
feat.caravan-leader.text: You know how to get the most effort out of your allies on the road. Your group can [[action.hustle|Hustle]] for an additional 20 minutes beyond the length of time that the member who could Hustle longest on their own.
feat.cast-down.name: Cast Down
feat.cast-down.text: The sheer force of your faith can bring a foe crashing down. If the next action you use is to cast [[spell.harm|_harm_]] or [[spell.heal|_heal_]] to damage one creature, the target is knocked [[condition.prone|prone]] if it takes any damage from the spell. If the target critically fails its save against the spell, it also takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speed for 1 minute.
feat.castigating-weapon.name: Castigating Weapon
feat.castigating-weapon.text: The force of your deity’s castigation strengthens your body so you can strike down the enemy and its allies. After you deal spirit damage due to Divine Castigation, your weapon or unarmed Strikes gain your holy or unholy trait and deal additional spirit damage until the end of your turn. The spirit damage is equal to the rank of harm or heal you dealt spirit damage with, and is in addition to any spirit damage the weapon already deals (such as from a holy rune).
feat.cat-fall.name: Cat Fall
feat.cat-fall.text: Your catlike aerial acrobatics allow you to cushion your falls. Treat falls as 10 feet shorter. If you’re an expert in Acrobatics, treat falls as 25 feet shorter and 50 feet if you’re a master. If you’re legendary in Acrobatics, you always land on your feet and don’t take damage, regardless of the distance of the fall.
feat.cat-nap.name: Cat Nap
feat.cat-nap.text: You can regain your energy quickly with a brief nap. You sleep for 10 minutes, after which you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 hour.
feat.caterwaul.name: Caterwaul
feat.caterwaul.text: You give a daring yowl, calling your companion back from the brink of unconsciousness. Your ally isn't knocked out and remains at 1 Hit Point. Their [[condition.wounded|wounded]] condition still increases by 1 as though they had been dying and recovered.
feat.caterwaul.trigger: An ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 HP but not immediately killed.
feat.catfolk-dance.name: Catfolk Dance
feat.catfolk-dance.text:
You have a habit of always being in the way when other creatures attempt to move. Attempt an [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] check against an adjacent creature's Reflex DC.

**Critical Success** The target creature gains a –2 circumstance penalty to Reflex saves and is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] until the start of your next turn.

**Success** The target creature gains a –2 circumstance penalty to Reflex saves until the start of your next turn.
feat.catfolk-lore.name: Catfolk Lore
feat.catfolk-lore.text:
Growing up among catfolk has taught you the traditional values of freedom, stewardship, and quick reactions to trouble. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] and [[skill.survival|Survival]]. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You also gain the [[feat.additional-lore|Additional Lore]] general feat for [[skill.lore|Catfolk Lore]].
feat.catfolk-weapon-familiarity.name: Catfolk Weapon Familiarity
feat.catfolk-weapon-familiarity.text:
You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the [[trait.catfolk|catfolk]] trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the catfolk trait plus the [[item.kama|kama]], [[item.kukri|kukri]], [[item.scimitar|scimitar]], and [[item.sickle|sickle]]—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.
feat.cats-luck.name: Cat's Luck
feat.cats-luck.text: You instinctively twist away from danger. Reroll the triggering saving throw and use the better result.
feat.cats-luck.trigger: You fail a Reflex saving throw
feat.cauldron.name: Cauldron
feat.cauldron.text:
You can brew magic in your cauldron, creating useful magical concoctions. You can use the Craft activity to create oils and potions. You immediately gain the formulas for four common 1st-level oils or potions. At 4th level and every 2 levels beyond that, you gain the formula for a common oil or potion of that level or lower (a 4th-level potion if you’re 4th level, a 6th-level potion if you’re 6th level, and so on). If you have a familiar, you can have your familiar learn these formulas rather than storing them in a formula book. Your familiar can learn new formulas in the same way it learns new spells, and these formulas are transferred from a slain familiar to a new familiar in the same way spells are.

During your daily preparations, you can create one temporary oil or potion using a formula you know. If you have master proficiency in spell DC, you can create a batch of two temporary oils or potions during your daily preparations, and if you have legendary proficiency, you can create a batch of three. Any items you create this way become inert bottles of liquid the next time you make your daily preparations, and any remaining effects of the temporary items end. A temporary oil or potion has no value.
feat.cautious-curiosity.name: Cautious Curiosity
feat.cautious-curiosity.prereq.0: at least one arcane or occult innate spell gained from a gnome heritage or gnome ancestry feat
feat.cautious-curiosity.text: You've learned a few magical techniques for getting yourself both into and out of trouble unnoticed. You gain [[spell.disguise-magic|_disguise magic_]] and [[spell.silence|_silence_]] as 2nd-rank arcane or occult innate spells. The tradition of these spells must match the tradition you use for your gnome ancestry options. You can cast each spell once per day and can target only yourself.
feat.cavalier-dedication.name: Cavalier Dedication
feat.cavalier-dedication.text:
You gain a young animal companion that serves as your mount. You can choose from animal companions with the mount special ability, as well as any additional options from your pledge (see Cavalier Pledges sidebar), as determined by your GM. You must choose an animal companion that’s at least one size larger than you, but if the animal usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).

**Special** If you have pledged yourself to a cause, you can take a second dedication feat closely tied to that cause even if you haven’t taken two additional cavalier feats. For instance, if you pledged yourself to fight crime with a group of vigilantes, you could take the vigilante dedication without first completing the cavalier archetype. The GM determines what archetypes, if any, are valid choices.

**Cavalier Pledges**

Many cavaliers pledge themselves in service to a specific organization or individual, such as a noble family or sovereign ruler, a knightly order or another organization, or particular ideal. A cavalier pledged to an order or ideal must uphold its edicts and is beholden to any anathema it has; for example, a cavalier pledged to the druid's animal order would be tied to that anathema, while a cavalier pledged to a deity's church would be held to the same standards as a cleric of that god. If you pledge yourself to an entity or cause without a stated anathema, you should work with your GM to determine the edicts and anathema associated with your pledge. Cavaliers who have pledged themselves can gain access to certain abilities related to that pledge, such as Cavalier's Banner. If you violate the anathema of your pledge, you lose access to those feats until you benefit from an [[ritual.atone|_atone_]] ritual. Changing the subject of your pledge is equivalent to retraining a class feature.
feat.cavaliers-banner.name: Cavalier's Banner
feat.cavaliers-banner.requirements: You have pledged your service to a specific organization or ideal.
feat.cavaliers-banner.text: You fly the banner of your pledge from your mount, raising your allies’ spirits. You and all allies in a 30-foot emanation from your mount gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects. If your banner is destroyed or removed, allies within 30 feet become [[condition.frightened|frightened]] 1.
feat.cavaliers-charge.name: Cavalier's Charge
feat.cavaliers-charge.text: You [[action.command-an-animal|Command an Animal]] to order your mount to [[action.stride|Stride]] twice. At any point during this movement, you can [[action.strike|Strike]] one enemy within reach or within the first range increment of a ranged weapon. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll.
feat.cave-climber.name: Cave Climber
feat.cave-climber.text: After years of clambering through caverns, you can climb easily anywhere you go. You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.
feat.ceaseless-shadows.name: Ceaseless Shadows
feat.ceaseless-shadows.text: You excel at going unnoticed, especially among a crowd. You no longer need to have cover or be [[condition.concealed|concealed]] to [[action.hide|Hide]] or [[action.sneak|Sneak]]. If you would have lesser cover from a creature, you gain standard cover instead and can [[action.take-cover|Take Cover]]; if you would have standard cover from a creature, you gain greater cover instead.
feat.celebrity-dedication.name: Celebrity Dedication
feat.celebrity-dedication.text: The more people you have looking at you, the more content you are, and you take every opportunity to show up others when their performances are less than perfect. You gain the Upstage reaction. In addition, when you Earn Income, if the level of the task is higher than your level, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check to Earn Income.
feat.celestial-magic.name: Celestial Magic
feat.celestial-magic.prereq.0: Angelkin, Lawbringer, Musetouched, or or another lineage feat associated with celestials
feat.celestial-magic.text: You possess celestial magic. Choose two of the following spells: [[spell.clear-mind|_clear mind_]], [[spell.everlight|_everlight_]], [[spell.humanoid-form|_humanoid form_]], [[spell.revealing-light|_revealing light_]], [[spell.share-life|_share life_]], or [[spell.sure-footing|_sure footing_]]. You can use each of the chosen spells once per day as 2nd-rank divine innate spells. [[feat.angelkin|Angelkin]] typically take clear mind and humanoid form, [[feat.lawbringer|lawbringers]] typically have everlight and share life, and [[feat.musetouched|musetouched]] typically have revealing light and sure footing.
feat.celestial-mercy.name: Celestial Mercy
feat.celestial-mercy.prereq.0: Angelkin, Lawbringer, Musetouched, or another lineage feat associated with celestials
feat.celestial-mercy.text: Your celestial powers allow you to remove lesser afflictions with ease. You can cast [[spell.cleanse-affliction|_cleanse affliction_]] twice per day as a 4th-rank divine innate spell.
feat.ceremonial-knife.name: Ceremonial Knife
feat.ceremonial-knife.text:
You have prepared a special knife to direct energies when spellcasting. During your daily preparations, you and your familiar can perform a short ritual over a weapon in the knife group—typically a dagger. This causes the knife to function as a magic wand, containing any one 1st-rank spell your familiar knows. You, and only you, can Activate the knife to Cast the Spell within it, as normal for a wand. You can attempt to overcharge the knife, and this can break or destroy the knife as normal. You can have only one ceremonial knife at a time.

At 8th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the maximum rank of spell your ceremonial knife can hold increases by 1.
feat.certain-stratagem.name: Certain Stratagem
feat.certain-stratagem.text: You know exactly where to strike a foe to target their weak spots. When you make a Strike that you're adding your Intelligence modifier to due to [[action.devise-a-stratagem|Devising a Stratagem]] and miss, you deal half of your strategic strike damage to the target. This damage type is that of the weapon or unarmed attack you used for the Strike.
feat.certain-strike.name: Certain Strike
feat.certain-strike.text:
Even when you don’t hit squarely, you can still score a glancing blow. Make a melee Strike. It gains the following failure effect.

**Failure** Your attack deals any damage it would have dealt on a hit, excluding all damage dice. (This removes damage dice from weapon runes, spells, and special abilities, in addition to weapon damage dice.)
feat.champion-dedication.name: Champion Dedication
feat.champion-dedication.text:
Choose a deity. You are bound by your deity’s anathema and gain the champion’s aura and sanctification as described in the [[class.champion|champion]] class. Choose a cause as you would if you were a champion, with the same options a champion must abide by. You gain its edicts and anathema but don’t gain the other abilities.

You become trained in [[skill.religion|Religion]] and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in champion class DC. If you later gain a devotion spell, you become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC.

You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well.
