feat.tangled-forest-stance.text:
You extend your arms like gnarled branches to interfere with your foes' movements. You can make lashing branch unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the [[trait.agile|agile]], [[trait.finesse|finesse]], [[trait.nonlethal|nonlethal]], and [[trait.unarmed|unarmed]] traits.

While you're in Tangled Forest Stance and can act, every enemy in your reach that tries to move away from you must succeed at a Reflex save, [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] check, or [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check against your class DC or be [[condition.immobilized|immobilized]] for that action. If you prefer, you can allow the enemy to move.
feat.tap-into-blood.name: Tap Into Blood
feat.tap-into-blood.requirements: You are benefiting from a blood magic effect
feat.tap-into-blood.text:
The power in your blood allows you to perform minor feats of magic. You can perform one of the following actions depending on the tradition of your bloodline. 
- **[[trait.arcane|Arcane]]** Your mind temporarily opens to the secrets of the world. Attempt to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]]; you can use [[skill.arcana|Arcana]] instead of the skill normally needed for that subject. If you critically fail at this check, you get a failure instead.
- [[trait.divine|**Divine**]] Whatever divine provenance is in your lineage guides you to instinctively move yourself or others out of harm's way. You [[action.step|Step]], or you [[action.reposition|Reposition]] a target within your reach using [[skill.religion|Religion]] for the check.
- [[trait.occult|**Occult**]] Strange mists or swirling colors hide your movement. You [[action.step|Step]] up to 10 feet.
- [[trait.primal|**Primal**]] The immense power of nature echoes in your voice. You can attempt a [[skill.nature|Nature]] check to [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]] a target.
feat.target-of-opportunity.name: Target of Opportunity
feat.target-of-opportunity.requirements: You have a ranged or thrown weapon in hand.
feat.target-of-opportunity.text: You capitalize on your ally’s attack and use the opportunity to secure a blow of your own, adding to the oncoming barrage. Make a ranged [[action.strike|Strike]] with a –2 penalty against the opponent targeted by the triggering attack. This Strike doesn’t count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t apply to this Strike. If this Strike is successful, combine the damage from the attack with the damage from your ally’s attack for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.
feat.target-of-opportunity.trigger: An ally succeeds at a ranged [[action.strike|Strike]] against an opponent in your weapon’s first range increment.
feat.targeting-finisher.name: Targeting Finisher
feat.targeting-finisher.text:
Your attack harms and hinders your foe. Choose a particular part of your foe from the list below and Strike. If you hit and damage the target, apply the effect corresponding to the chosen part. This hindrance lasts until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, you also apply a lesser effect lasting for 1 minute. 
- **Arm** (or another limb used for attacks, such as a tentacle) The target is [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled 2]]. On a critical hit, it is also enfeebled 1 for 1 minute.
- **Head** The target is [[condition.stupefied|stupefied 2]]. On a critical hit, it is also stupefied 1 for 1 minute.
- **Legs** The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds. On a critical hit, it also takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute.
feat.telluric-power.name: Telluric Power
feat.telluric-power.text: You channel strength from the earth beneath your feet to pummel your enemies. When making a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] against a target who is standing on the same earth or stone surface as you are, you gain a circumstance bonus to the damage roll equal to the number of weapon damage dice.
feat.ten-lives.name: Ten Lives
feat.ten-lives.text: When your character would die, you can attempt a DC 17 flat check. On a success, you're instead reduced to 0 HP and a [[condition.dying|dying]] value 1 less than what would normally kill you (typically dying 3). This doesn't change the result for any other creature affected.
feat.tenacious-net.name: Tenacious Net
feat.tenacious-net.text: Escaping your nets is no simple task. The [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] DC to [[action.force-open|Force Open]] or [[action.escape|Escape]] your nets increases from 16 to 18. After a creature you [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]] with a net Escapes or Forces Open the net, stray strands of the net cling to the creature, causing them to remain [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] until the beginning of their next turn.
feat.tenacious-toxins.name: Tenacious Toxins
feat.tenacious-toxins.text: Your victims tend to expire long before your poisons, since the latter have been specifically formulated to last longer. The maximum duration of any poison you create increases by an amount equal to the poison's stage 1 interval, to a maximum of twice the poison's maximum duration.
feat.tengu-feather-fan.name: Tengu Feather Fan
feat.tengu-feather-fan.text:
You've learned to bind some of your feathers together into a fan to focus your ancestral magic. You gain a tengu feather fan: a magic item of light Bulk with a level equal to your level and the [[trait.primal|primal]] trait. You (and only you) can cast tengu magic with the Wave Fan activation. If your fan is lost or destroyed, you can create a replacement during your daily preparations; if you do so, your previous fan falls apart into mundane feathers. Your tengu feather fan contains a 1st-rank [[spell.gust-of-wind|_gust of wind_]] spell. Further feats might add more spells and grant you additional activations of your tengu feather fan, but you can never have more than three activations per day, no matter how many such feats you have.

**Activate—Wave Fan** {1a} ([[trait.manipulate|manipulate]]) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast your choice of one spell contained in your tengu feather fan. You can instead cast a cantrip you've gained from a heritage or an ancestry feat; this doesn't use up one of the fan's daily activations.

This activation takes the spell's normal number of actions. The spell's DC is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
feat.tengu-lore.name: Tengu Lore
feat.tengu-lore.text:
You learned skills for surviving in the place where your people were dispersed. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [[skill.society|Society]] and [[skill.survival|Survival]]. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You also gain the [[feat.additional-lore|Additional Lore]] general feat for [[skill.lore|Tengu Lore]].
feat.tengu-weapon-familiarity.name: Tengu Weapon Familiarity
feat.tengu-weapon-familiarity.text:
You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the [[trait.tengu|tengu]] trait plus the [[item.katana|katana]], [[item.khakkhara|khakkara]], [[item.temple-sword|temple sword]], and [[item.wakizashi|wakizashi]]. You have familiarity with these weapons—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

During your daily preparations, you can practice with a weapon from the sword group that's in your possession. You gain familiarity with that weapon as well. This lasts until you practice with a different sword in the same way.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.
feat.terraforming-trickery.name: Terraforming Trickery
feat.terraforming-trickery.text:
You know how to channel the transformative aspects of your blood magic to alter your surroundings. You know the following blood magic effect. 
**Blood Magic—Terraforming Trickery** Either each space adjacent to you becomes difficult terrain, or each space adjacent to you is no longer difficult terrain. This doesn't have any effect on greater difficult terrain and doesn't remove the damaging effects of hazardous terrain.
feat.terrain-advantage.name: Terrain Advantage
feat.terrain-advantage.text: Non-[[trait.lizardfolk|lizardfolk]] creatures in difficult terrain are [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] to you. If you have a swim Speed, non-lizardfolk creatures that are in water and lack a swim Speed are also off-guard to you.
feat.terrain-expertise.name: Terrain Expertise
feat.terrain-expertise.text:
Your experience in navigating a certain type of terrain makes you supremely confident while doing so. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks in one of the following types of terrain, chosen when you select this feat: aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, swamp, or underground.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different type of terrain each time.
feat.terrain-master.name: Terrain Master
feat.terrain-master.text: You are able to adapt to your surroundings in any natural terrain. You can spend 1 hour practicing in your current terrain in order to make it your favored terrain, replacing your current favored terrain temporarily. If you spend a full day out of the new favored terrain, your favored terrain reverts back to your original choice when you took the Favored Terrain feat.
feat.terrain-scout.name: Terrain Scout
feat.terrain-scout.text: You have mastered movement in many different environments. You gain the [[feat.terrain-stalker|Terrain Stalker]] skill feat twice, choosing a different terrain each time. If you [[action.avoid-notice|Avoid Notice]] while exploring and any allies use [[action.follow-the-expert|Follow the Expert]] to follow you as you do so, you can choose one of those allies to gain the benefit of any one Terrain Stalker feat you have.
feat.terrain-stalker.name: Terrain Stalker
feat.terrain-stalker.text:
Select one type of difficult terrain from the following list: rubble, snow, or underbrush. While undetected by all non-allies in that type of terrain, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than 5 feet and do not pass within 10 feet of an enemy during your movement.

During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren’t actively Searching or on guard.

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different type of terrain.
feat.terrified-retreat.name: Terrified Retreat
feat.terrified-retreat.text: When you critically succeed at the Demoralize action, if the target's level is lower than yours, the target is [[condition.fleeing|fleeing]] for 1 round.
feat.terrifying-croak.name: Terrifying Croak
feat.terrifying-croak.text: You release a haunting croak that reminds those around you of their fears. Attempt an Intimidation check to [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]] a creature within 30 feet; you do not take a penalty to this check for not speaking a language. If the check is successful, the target cannot reduce their [[condition.frightened|frightened]] condition below 1 for 1 round.
feat.terrifying-howl.name: Terrifying Howl
feat.terrifying-howl.text: You unleash a terrifying howl. Attempt [[skill.intimidation|Intimidation]] checks to [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]] each enemy within 30 feet: you don't take a penalty if the creature doesn't understand your language. Regardless of the results of your checks, each target is then temporarily immune to Terrifying Howl for 1 minute.
feat.terrifying-resistance.name: Terrifying Resistance
feat.terrifying-resistance.text: The spells of those you have [[action.demoralize|Demoralized]] are less effective on you. If you succeed in Demoralizing a creature, for the next 24 hours you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that creature's spells.
feat.thats-odd.name: That's Odd
feat.thats-odd.text:
When you enter a new location, such as a room or corridor, you immediately notice one thing out of the ordinary. The GM determines what it is, or whether there's nothing reasonable to pick up, skipping obvious clues that can be easily noticed without a check or specifically looking for them. You learn only that an area or object is suspicious, but not why it's suspicious. For example, if you entered a study with a large bloodstain on the ground, the bloodstain is so obviously suspicious it's evident to you already, so the GM might note that there's something suspicious about the desk drawer instead. You would then need to investigate the drawer further to find out what specifically is out of the ordinary. If you wish, you can [[action.pursue-a-lead|Pursue a Lead]] concerning this detail even if you have Pursed a Lead less than 10 minutes ago.

That's Odd doesn't reveal whether creatures are suspicious. You don't typically get any benefit when you leave and come back to a place, though if a major change has happened there and time has passed, the GM might determine that you do.
feat.the-bigger-they-are.name: The Bigger They Are
feat.the-bigger-they-are.text:
With reckless speed, you dash, jump and swing around a creature to find a more vulnerable spot. Attempt to [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] a creature at least one size category larger than you, using the following effects.

**Critical Success** You move through the enemy's space, treating the squares in its space as difficult terrain (every 5 feet costs 10 feet of movement). If you don't have enough Speed to move all the way through its space, you get the same effect as a failure. If you successfully pass through the target's square, the target gains weakness to your precision damage equal to half your level, which lasts until the end of your turn.

**Success** As success, but the weakness applies only against the next attack you make against the target.

**Failure** Your movement ends, and you trigger reactions as if you had moved out of the square you started in.

**Critical Failure** As failure, and you fall [[condition.prone|prone]].
feat.the-dead-walk.name: The Dead Walk
feat.the-dead-walk.text: You beseech warrior spirits to come forth and aid you. Two ghostly warriors manifest within a 30-foot emanation of you and each attempt a [[action.strike|Strike]] against an adjacent enemy, using your spell attack modifier. The warriors' Strikes each deal 4d6 [[trait.spirit|spirit]] damage and the warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies. If you are [[trait.cursebound|cursebound]] 2 when you use The Dead Walk, you instead summon three warriors, and if you are cursebound 3, you instead summon four warriors. The warriors disappear at the start of your next turn.
feat.the-harder-they-fall-rogue.name: The Harder They Fall
feat.the-harder-they-fall-rogue.text: You make your foes fall painfully when you trip them. When you successfully Trip an off-guard foe, your target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage. On a critical success, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage plus your sneak attack damage.
feat.thorned-seedpod.name: Thorned Seedpod
feat.thorned-seedpod.text: When your seedpods [[action.strike|strike]] a felling blow, they burst into viciously thorny vines. When you critically succeed at a seedpod Strike, vines twist and stab your foe, dealing 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent]] piercing damage.
feat.thorough-research.name: Thorough Research
feat.thorough-research.text: You have comprehensive knowledge in your fields of interest. When you succeed at a [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] check, you gain additional information or context. When you critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge, you get additional information or context or can ask an additional follow-up question (the GM chooses which).
feat.thorough-search.name: Thorough Search
feat.thorough-search.text: You take your time searching to ensure you find everything. When [[action.search|Searching]], you can take twice as long to search. Normally this means you Search at up to one quarter of your Speed, to a maximum of 150 feet per minute to check everything, or 75 feet per minute to check everything before you walk into an area. If you do and the GM rolls your secret check to Seek to notice something, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to that Perception check and if you succeed, you get a critical success instead.
feat.thousand-visions.name: Thousand Visions
feat.thousand-visions.text: You open your senses to numerous visions of the immediate future. The visions grant you subtle details of your immediate surroundings within 30 feet. Within this range, you don't need to succeed at a flat check to target a concealed creature, you're not [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] to creatures that are [[condition.hidden|hidden]] from you (unless you're off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful DC 5 flat check to target a hidden creature. Beyond 30 feet, the visions become overwhelmed with too many possible futures, making all of your senses imprecise beyond this range. The visions persist for 1 minute.
feat.thrash.name: Thrash
feat.thrash.text: You thrash your foe around. An enemy you have [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]] or [[condition.restrained|restrained]] takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier plus your weapon specialization damage plus your [[action.rage|Rage]] damage, with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC.
feat.thunder-gods-fan.name: Thunder God's Fan
feat.thunder-gods-fan.text: Your fan unleashes the fury of the storm. You can use the Wave Fan activation one additional time per day. Add a 5th-rank [[spell.lightning-bolt|_lightning bolt_]] spell to the spells contained within your fan.
feat.thunderclap-spell.name: Thunderclap Spell
feat.thunderclap-spell.text: Your lightning splits the air, generating a booming shock wave. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that has the electricity trait or deals electricity damage, has no duration, and requires creatures to attempt a saving throw, the force of the spell’s lightning creates a thunderclap, in addition to its other effects. Each creature that failed its Reflex save against the spell is deafened for 1 round, and those who critically failed are also knocked prone.
feat.tiger-slash.name: Tiger Slash
feat.tiger-slash.text: You make a fierce swipe with both hands. Make a tiger claw Strike. It deals two extra weapon damage dice (three extra dice if you're 14th level or higher), and you can push the target 5 feet away as if you had successfully [[action.shove|Shoved]] them. If the attack is a critical success and deals damage, add your Strength modifier to the [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]] from your tiger claw.
feat.tiger-stance.name: Tiger Stance
feat.tiger-stance.text:
You enter the stance of a tiger and can make tiger claw attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the [[trait.agile|agile]], [[trait.finesse|finesse]], [[trait.nonlethal|nonlethal]], and [[trait.unarmed|unarmed]] traits. On a critical success with your tiger claws, if you deal damage, the target takes 1d4 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]].

As long as your Speed is at least 20 feet while in Tiger Stance, you can Step 10 feet.
feat.timeless-nature.name: Timeless Nature
feat.timeless-nature.text: With primal magic sustaining you, you cease aging. The overflowing primal energy gives you a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and primal magic.
feat.tinkering-fingers.name: Tinkering Fingers
feat.tinkering-fingers.text: You're trained in [[skill.crafting|Crafting]]. If you are trained in Crafting from another source (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can [[action.repair|Repair]] an item without using a [[item.repair-toolkit|repair toolkit]] without taking the –2 circumstance penalty, improvising tools from whatever you have at hand. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Repair an item when you have a repair toolkit.
feat.titan-slinger.name: Titan Slinger
feat.titan-slinger.text: You have learned how to use your sling to fell enormous creatures. When you hit on an attack with a weapon of the sling group against a Large or larger creature, increase the size of the weapon damage die by one step (details on increasing weapon damage die sizes can be found on page 276).
feat.titan-wrestler.name: Titan Wrestler
feat.titan-wrestler.text: You can attempt to Disarm, Grapple, Reposition, Shove, or Trip creatures up to two sizes larger than you, or up to three sizes larger than you if you’re legendary in Athletics.
feat.titans-stature.name: Titan's Stature
feat.titans-stature.text: You grow to even greater size. When using Giant's Stature, you can instead become Huge (increasing your [[trait.reach|reach]] by 10 feet if you were Medium or smaller).
feat.to-battle.name: To Battle!
feat.to-battle.text: With a resounding cry, you rally your ally to take the offensive. Choose one ally in your marshal’s aura who has a reaction available. If you spend 1 action, that ally can use their reaction to immediately [[action.stride|Stride]]. If you spend 2 actions, that ally can use their reaction to immediately [[action.strike|Strike]].
feat.to-the-ends-of-the-earth.name: To the Ends of the Earth
feat.to-the-ends-of-the-earth.text: Your ability to track your prey has surpassed explanation, allowing you to trace your prey’s movements and predict its location with ease. When you use Hunt Prey on a creature within 100 feet, you can follow that creature’s movements, allowing you to know the creature’s exact location no matter how far away it becomes, as long as it remains your prey. You must be legendary in Nature to track your prey’s location across teleportation or planar travel. This feat gains the detection and primal traits if you’re legendary in Nature.
feat.tongue-tether.name: Tongue Tether
feat.tongue-tether.text: Your tongue can momentarily latch on as readily as your hands. So long as you can freely open your mouth, you do not need free hands in order to [[action.disarm|Disarm]], [[action.grab-an-edge|Grab an Edge]], [[action.reposition|Reposition]], or [[action.trip|Trip]]. If you have the [[feat.long-tongue|Long Tongue]] feat, you can Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition, and Trip with your tongue at a distance that is 5 feet beyond your normal reach.
feat.tools-of-the-trade.name: Tools of the Trade
feat.tools-of-the-trade.text: You’re well-versed in weapons that allow you to bring bounties back in one piece, or at least alive. You have familiarity with the bola, sap, and whip; for the purposes of proficiency, you treat these weapons as simple weapons. You deal an additional 1d4 precision damage with these weapons when using them to make nonlethal Strikes against your prey while they’re off-guard to you. In addition, you take no penalty when making a nonlethal attack with a weapon without the nonlethal trait.
feat.topple-foe.name: Topple Foe
feat.topple-foe.text: You take advantage of the opening created by your ally to tip your foe off their feet. Attempt an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.trip|Trip]] the target of the triggering attack.
feat.topple-foe.trigger: An ally succeeds at a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] against an enemy you are both adjacent to.
feat.toppling-dance.name: Toppling Dance
feat.toppling-dance.text: While sharing a creature's space using Dance Underfoot, your melee weapons and unarmed attacks gain the [[trait.trip|trip]] trait, but only against the creature whose space you share. You can be in the same space as a Large or larger prone creature, even if it's not your ally.
feat.toughness.name: Toughness
feat.toughness.text: Your body can withstand more punishment than most before succumbing. Increase your maximum Hit Points by your level. You reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1.
feat.traditional-resistances.name: Traditional Resistances
feat.traditional-resistances.prereq.0: Arcane Dragonblood, Divine Dragonblood, Occult Dragonblood, or Primal Dragonblood
feat.traditional-resistances.text: Due to your blood, you have some resistance to certain types of magic. You gain a +1 status bonus to AC and saves against spells and other magical effects from the same tradition as your lineage. This bonus increases to +2 against [[trait.sleep|sleep]] and [[condition.paralyzed|paralysis]] effects.
feat.train-animal.name: Train Animal
feat.train-animal.text:
You spend time teaching an animal to do a certain action. You can either select a basic action the animal already knows how to do (typically those listed in the Command an Animal action on page 242) or attempt to teach the animal a new basic action. The GM determines the DC of any check required and the amount of time the training takes (usually at least a week). It’s usually impossible to teach an animal a trick that uses critical thinking. If you’re expert, master, or legendary in Nature, you might be able to train more unusual creatures, at the GM’s discretion.

**Success** The animal learns the action. If it was an action the animal already knew, you can Command the Animal to take that action without attempting a Nature check. If it was a new basic action, add that action to the actions the animal can take when Commanded, but you must still roll.

**Failure** The animal doesn’t learn the trick.
feat.trampling-charge.name: Trampling Charge
feat.trampling-charge.requirements: You are riding a mount that has a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] using its legs (claw, talons, hoof, etc.).
feat.trampling-charge.text: You urge your mount to charge into the fray, trampling all enemies who stand in your path. You command your mount to [[action.stride|Stride]] up to double its Speed (or to [[action.burrow|Burrow]], [[action.climb|Climb]], [[action.fly|Fly]], or [[action.swim|Swim]], if it has the corresponding movement type), moving through the spaces of any foes in your path up to one size smaller than your mount. Your mount deals the damage of one of its melee Strikes to each creature whose space you move through, with a basic Reflex save against your mount’s [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] DC. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes off-guard until the end of your next turn. Roll the damage only once. You can damage a given creature only once during this movement.
feat.trap-finder.name: Trap Finder
feat.trap-finder.text:
You have an intuitive sense that alerts you to the presence of traps. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps, to AC against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps. Even if you aren’t Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

You can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of master in Thievery. If you have master proficiency in Thievery, you can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of legendary instead, and your circumstance bonuses against traps increase to +2.
feat.treat-condition.name: Treat Condition
feat.treat-condition.requirements: You are holding [[item.healers-toolkit-expanded|healer's tools]], or you are wearing them and have a hand free.
feat.treat-condition.text:
You treat an adjacent creature in an attempt to reduce the [[condition.clumsy|clumsy]], [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled]], or [[condition.sickened|sickened]] condition. If a creature has multiple conditions from this list, choose one. Attempt a counteract check against the condition using your [[skill.medicine|Medicine]] modifier as your counteract modifier and the condition’s source to determine the DC. You can’t treat a condition that came from an [[trait.artifact|artifact]] or effect above 20th level unless you have [[feat.legendary-medic|Legendary Medic]]; even if you do, the counteract DC increases by 10. Treating a Condition that is continually applied under certain circumstances (for instance, the enfeebled condition a [[trait.holy|holy]] character gains from carrying a weapon with the unholy rune) has no effect as long as the circumstances continue.

**Critical Success** Reduce the condition value by 2.

**Success** Reduce the condition value by 1.

**Critical Failure** Increase the condition value by 1.
feat.tree-climber.name: Tree Climber
feat.tree-climber.text: You've spent much of your life among the treetops and have become an expert at quickly and safely climbing them. You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.
feat.trial-by-skyfire.name: Trial by Skyfire
feat.trial-by-skyfire.text: Your lips murmur as you portend a great disaster, one you hope you survive. A rain of blazing bolts begins to fall from the sky in a 10-foot emanation, centered on you, that deals 2d6 fire damage to all creatures in the emanation at the end of each of your turns (basic Reflex save); you can't exclude yourself from the emanation. The skyfire persists for 1 minute; while you can't [[action.dismiss|Dismiss]] it, you can suppress the effect for 1 round with a [[action.sustain|Sustain]] action. The rain of fire is suppressed if you fall [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]]. If you become [[trait.cursebound|cursebound]] 3 or 4 at any point during Trial by Skyfire's duration, the emanation increases to 15 feet and the damage increases to 4d6.
feat.triangle-shot.name: Triangle Shot
feat.triangle-shot.requirements: You are in Monastic Archer Stance and wielding a bow usable with that stance.
feat.triangle-shot.text: You string three arrows to your bow and fire them all at once. Make three ranged Strikes against a single target with the required weapon, each using your current multiple attack penalty, and you take an additional –2 penalty. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty, and you combine the attacks' damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Your [[feat.stunning-blows|Stunning Blows]] benefit applies to Triangle Shot, even though it isn't a [[action.flurry-of-blows|Flurry of Blows]]. If all three Strikes hit, the target takes 3d6 [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent bleed damage]].
feat.trick-magic-item.name: Trick Magic Item
feat.trick-magic-item.text:
You examine a magic item you normally couldn’t use in an effort to fool it and activate it temporarily. For example, this might allow a fighter to cast a spell from a wand or allow a wizard to cast a spell that’s not on the arcane list using a scroll. You must know what activating the item does, or you can’t attempt to trick it.

Attempt a check using the skill matching the item’s magic tradition, or matching a tradition that has the spell on its list, if you’re trying to cast a spell from the item. The relevant skills are Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, Religion for divine, or any of the four for an item that has the magical trait and not a tradition trait. The GM determines the DC based on the item’s level (possibly adjusted depending on the item or situation).

If you activate a magic item that requires a spell attack modifier or spell DC and you don’t have proficiency in the relevant statistic, use your level as your proficiency bonus and the highest of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifiers. If you’re a master in the appropriate skill for the item’s tradition, you instead use the trained proficiency bonus; if you’re legendary, you instead use the expert proficiency bonus.

**Success** For the rest of the current turn, you can spend actions to activate the item as if you could normally use it.

**Failure** You can’t use the item or try to trick it again this turn, but you can try again on subsequent turns.

**Critical Failure** You can’t use the item, and you can’t try to trick it again until your next daily preparations.
feat.trickster-tengu.name: Trickster Tengu
feat.trickster-tengu.text: You can transform yourself or the bodies of others to express your displeasure. Once per day, you can cast either [[spell.aerial-form|_aerial form_]] or [[spell.cursed-metamorphosis|_cursed metamorphosis_]] as a 7th-rank primal innate spell. You must take the form of a bird when casting this aerial form.
feat.tricksters-ace.name: Trickster's Ace
feat.tricksters-ace.requirements: When you make your daily preparations, you must specify a trigger for this reaction using the same restrictions as the triggers for the [[action.ready|Ready]] action. You also choose a single spell from the arcane, divine, occult, or primal list of 4th level or lower. The spell can’t have a cost, nor can its casting time be more than 10 minutes. The spell must be able to target a single creature, and you must be a valid target for it.
feat.tricksters-ace.text: Whether from jury-rigged magic items, deduction from the study of magical interactions, or other means, you have a contingency in your back pocket for desperate situations. When the trigger occurs, you cause the spell to come into effect. The spell targets only you, no matter how many creatures it would affect normally. If you define particularly complicated conditions, as determined by the GM, the trigger might fail. Once the contingency is triggered, the spell is expended until your next daily preparations.
feat.tricksters-ace.trigger: You specify the trigger when you make your daily preparations.
feat.tripkee-glide.name: Tripkee Glide
feat.tripkee-glide.requirements: You must have at least one hand free.
feat.tripkee-glide.text: You can use your webbed feet to guide your fall. You glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down (10 feet if you don't have both hands free) and up to 25 feet forward through the air. As long as you spend at least 1 action gliding each round and have not yet reached the ground, you remain in the air at the end of your turn.
feat.tripkee-lore.name: Tripkee Lore
feat.tripkee-lore.text:
You are well versed in tripkee culture and tactics. You gain the trained proficiency in [[skill.nature|Nature]] and [[skill.stealth|Stealth]]. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You also gain the [[feat.additional-lore|Additional Lore]] general feat for [[skill.lore|Tripkee Lore]].
feat.tripkee-weapon-familiarity.name: Tripkee Weapon Familiarity
feat.tripkee-weapon-familiarity.text:
You gain access to all [[trait.uncommon|uncommon]] weapons with the [[trait.tripkee|tripkee]] trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the tripkee trait plus the [[item.blowgun|blowgun]], [[item.dart|dart]], [[item.hatchet|hatchet]], [[item.scythe|scythe]], and [[item.shortbow|shortbow]]—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.
feat.triple-shot.name: Triple Shot
feat.triple-shot.text: You can quickly fire multiple shots with greater control. When you use Double Shot, you can make the attacks against the same target. You can add an additional action to Double Shot to make three ranged Strikes instead of two. If you do, the penalty is –4. All attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made all of them.
feat.triple-threat.name: Triple Threat
feat.triple-threat.text: You can divide your attention three ways when hunting. When you use Hunt Prey, you can designate three creatures as prey, designate two creatures as prey and share the effect with one ally (as Shared Prey), or designate one creature as prey and share the effect with two allies.
feat.triple-time.name: Triple Time
feat.triple-time.text: You learn the [[spell.triple-time|_triple time_]] composition cantrip, which speeds up you and your allies for a round.
feat.triumphant-inspiration.name: Triumphant Inspiration
feat.triumphant-inspiration.text: With a triumphant shout, you inspire your allies. You cast a [[trait.composition|composition]] cantrip you know that normally takes a single action to cast.
feat.triumphant-inspiration.trigger: You critically hit a foe with a melee weapon Strike or a melee unarmed attack
feat.true-debilitating-bomb.name: True Debilitating Bomb
feat.true-debilitating-bomb.text: You have discovered increasingly devastating ways for your bombs to impede your foes. When you use Debilitating Bomb, add the following to the list of effects you can choose from: [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled 2]], [[condition.stupefied|stupefied 2]], or a –15-foot status penalty to Speeds.
feat.true-dragons-flight.name: True Dragon's Flight
feat.true-dragons-flight.text: Your wings have grown more powerful, capable of keeping you aloft longer. You have a fly Speed of 20 feet at all times.
feat.true-hypercognition.name: True Hypercognition
feat.true-hypercognition.text: Your mind works at an incredible pace. You instantly use up to five [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] actions. If you have any special abilities or free actions that would normally be triggered when you Recall Knowledge, you can’t use them for these actions.
feat.true-perception.name: True Perception
feat.true-perception.text: Your perceptive abilities and ability to process sensory information are so far beyond the pale that you notice minute discrepancies in all sorts of illusions and physical transformations. You are constantly under the effects of a 6th rank [[spell.truesight|_truesight spell_]], using your Perception modifier for the counteract check.
feat.true-shapeshifter.name: True Shapeshifter
feat.true-shapeshifter.text:
You transcend the limitations of form. Once per day you can cast [[spell.nature-incarnate|_nature incarnate_]], even if you don’t have it prepared, to transform into a kaiju. If you have [[feat.plant-shape|Plant Shape]], you can choose to transform into a green man instead. You also gain the True Shapeshift activity.

**True Shapeshift** {2a} ([[trait.concentrate|concentrate]]) **Requirements** You’re under the effects of [[feat.untamed-form|untamed form]]; **Effect** You change into any other shape on your untamed form list. If the duration of that shape is different from the one you were previously in, use the shorter duration to determine your duration remaining.
feat.tumble-behind-rogue.name: Tumble Behind
feat.tumble-behind-rogue.text: You tumble under and behind your foe, your rapid movement letting you catch them off guard. When you successfully Tumble Through, the foe whose space you passed through is off-guard against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.
feat.tumble-behind-swashbuckler.name: Tumble Behind
feat.tumble-behind-swashbuckler.text: Your tumbling puts your foes on the back foot. When you [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] successfully, the foe you Tumbled Through is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.
feat.tumbling-diversion.name: Tumbling Diversion
feat.tumbling-diversion.text: Attempt to [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] an opponent's space. If you succeed or critically succeed and don't end your movement adjacent to that opponent, you can attempt to [[action.create-a-diversion|Create a Diversion]] to distract that opponent. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Deception check (or a +2 circumstance bonus if you critically succeeded at the Acrobatics check to Tumble Through) to Create a Diversion. If you succeed or critically succeed to Create a Diversion, you become [[condition.hidden|hidden]] to only the creature whose space you Tumbled Through.
feat.tumbling-opportunist.name: Tumbling Opportunist
feat.tumbling-opportunist.requirements: Your most recent action was to [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] or [[feat.tumbling-strike|Tumbling Strike]], and you successfully moved through an enemy’s space.
feat.tumbling-opportunist.text: You use a burst of stamina to perform a breathtaking feat of Acrobatics as you speed through a foe's space, leaving your foe lying flat on their back. You attempt to [[action.trip|Trip]] the enemy whose space you moved through. You can use [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] instead of [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] for this check.
feat.tumbling-strike.name: Tumbling Strike
feat.tumbling-strike.requirements: You are adjacent to an enemy.
feat.tumbling-strike.text:
You deftly dive through a gap left by a foe to deliver an advantageous blow. Attempt an [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] check against the Reflex DC of an enemy adjacent to you.

**Critical Success** You move through the enemy’s space to an unoccupied space on the other side of the enemy from your starting position. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions. You can’t move farther than your Speed, and you must end your movement adjacent to the enemy whose space you moved through. After moving, you make a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] against the enemy whose space you moved through, and the enemy is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] against that Strike.

**Success** As critical success, but the enemy isn’t off-guard against the Strike.

**Failure** You remain in your original space but can still Strike.

**Critical Failure** You neither move nor Strike.
feat.tumbling-teamwork.name: Tumbling Teamwork
feat.tumbling-teamwork.text: Your tumbling distracts a foe enough to create an advantage for one of your allies. When you successfully [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] an enemy's space, an ally who is adjacent to that enemy can [[action.step|Step]] as a reaction, but they must remain adjacent to that enemy.
feat.tumbling-theft.name: Tumbling Theft
feat.tumbling-theft.text: You reach for an opponent's item as you move past a foe. If you critically succeed at your check to [[action.tumble-through|Tumble Through]] an enemy's space, you can attempt to [[action.steal|Steal]] something from the enemy as a reaction. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Thievery check to Steal as your tumbling make it difficult for your enemy to keep track of your movement. You can Steal any immediately accessible item of light or negligible Bulk on the enemy's person, such as a potion or coin purse hanging from a belt, but not anything inside a container or anything the enemy is holding. The GM has final say on what you can Steal.
feat.tusks.name: Tusks
feat.tusks.text:
You have particularly long, jagged tusks perfect for tearing meat from bone. You gain a tusks unarmed attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. Your tusks are in the brawling group and have the [[trait.finesse|finesse]] and [[trait.unarmed|unarmed]] traits.

**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can’t retrain into this feat. You can retrain out of this feat only through drastic measures, such as breaking, filing, or extracting your tusks.
feat.twin-distraction.name: Twin Distraction
feat.twin-distraction.requirements: You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand
feat.twin-distraction.text: Your movements with two weapons are so swift and disorienting that they befuddle your opponent. When using Twin Feint, if both your Strikes deal damage to a targeted creature, the target must succeed at a Will saving throw against your class DC or become stupefied 1 until the end of your next turn.
feat.twin-feint.name: Twin Feint
feat.twin-feint.requirements: You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand
feat.twin-feint.text: You use an attack with one weapon to distract your foe from a second attack coming at a different angle. Make one Strike with each of your two melee weapons, both against the same target. The target is automatically off-guard against the second attack. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally.
feat.twin-parry.name: Twin Parry
feat.twin-parry.requirements: You are wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand
feat.twin-parry.text: You use your two weapons to parry attacks. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, or a +2 circumstance bonus if either weapon has the parry trait. You lose this circumstance bonus if you no longer meet this feat’s requirement.
feat.twin-riposte.name: Twin Riposte
feat.twin-riposte.requirements: You are benefiting from Twin Parry
feat.twin-riposte.text: A clever parry with one weapon leaves your opponent open to an attack with the other weapon. Make a melee Strike or Disarm action against the triggering opponent.
feat.twin-riposte.trigger: A creature within your reach critically fails to Strike you
feat.twin-takedown.name: Twin Takedown
feat.twin-takedown.requirements: You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand
feat.twin-takedown.text: You swiftly attack your hunted prey with each of your weapons, potentially combining their damage into a single devastating attack. Make two Strikes against your hunted prey, one with each of the required weapons. If both hit the same hunted prey, combine their damage for the purpose of its resistances and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.
feat.twinned-defense-fighter.name: Twinned Defense
feat.twinned-defense-fighter.requirement: You are wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand
feat.twinned-defense-fighter.text: You’re always ready to use your off-hand weapon to interfere with attacks against you. While you are in this stance, you constantly gain the benefits of the Twin Parry action.
feat.twirling-throw.name: Twirling Throw
feat.twirling-throw.text: Your thrown weapons seem to defy physics as they soar through the air and spin back to you after a strike. Make a [[trait.thrown|thrown]] weapon Strike, ignoring the penalty for making ranged attacks within the second and third range increment. The weapon returns to your hand after the attack unless you critically failed on the attack roll.
feat.twist-the-knife.name: Twist The Knife
feat.twist-the-knife.requirements: Your last action was a melee Strike that dealt sneak attack damage to an off-guard target
feat.twist-the-knife.text: After stabbing your opponent in a weak spot, you tear the wound open. You deal persistent bleed damage to the target equal to your number of sneak attack damage dice.
feat.two-weapon-flurry.name: Two-Weapon Flurry
feat.two-weapon-flurry.requirements: You are wielding two weapons, each in a different hand
feat.two-weapon-flurry.text: Using the momentum of your prior attack, you lash out with both your weapons in a sudden frenzy. Strike twice, once with each weapon.
feat.ultimate-flexibility.name: Ultimate Flexibility
feat.ultimate-flexibility.text:
Your experience keeps you on your toes, helping you adopt complex strategies on the fly and face the most dangerous challenges. When you gain a fighter feat using combat flexibility, you gain three fighter feats instead of two. While the first feat must still be 8th level or lower, the second feat can be up to 14th level, and the third feat can be up to 18th level.

You can use the first feat to meet the prerequisites of the second or third feats and the second feat to meet the prerequisites of the third feat. You must meet all three feats’ other prerequisites normally.

In addition, you can adapt to the battlefield’s challenges by spending 1 hour to train. If you do, you can reselect the feats chosen with combat flexibility as if you had made your daily preparations. You can’t trade out limited-use abilities that you’ve already used, such as Determination.
feat.ultimate-mercy.name: Ultimate Mercy
feat.ultimate-mercy.text: Your mercy transcends the bounds of life and death. Add ultimate mercy to the types of mercy you can provide. When you use Mercy, you can target a creature that died since your last turn to return it to life. The target returns to life with 1 Hit Point and becomes [[condition.wounded|wounded 1]]. You can't return the target to life if it died from [[spell.disintegrate|_disintegrate_]] or a [[trait.death|death]] effect. The creature gains the other benefits of lay on hands after it returns to life.
feat.ultimate-polymath.name: Ultimate Polymath
feat.ultimate-polymath.text: You can flexibly cast all of your spells, granting a dizzying array of possible options. All of the spells in your repertoire are signature spells for you.
feat.ultimate-skirmisher.name: Ultimate Skirmisher
feat.ultimate-skirmisher.text: You are so skilled at navigating the wild, your movement is completely unaffected by terrain. You ignore the effects of all difficult terrain, greater difficult terrain, and hazardous terrain, and you don’t trigger traps and hazards that are triggered by moving into an area (such as trip wires and pressure plates), unless you want to.
feat.unbalancing-blow.name: Unbalancing Blow
feat.unbalancing-blow.text: Interweaving attacks, you unbalance your foes. Whenever your Strike is a critical hit and deals damage, the target is offguard against your attacks until the end of your next turn.
feat.unbalancing-finisher.name: Unbalancing Finisher
feat.unbalancing-finisher.text: You attack with a flashy assault that leaves your target off balance. Make a melee Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] until the end of your next turn.
feat.unbalancing-sweep.name: Unbalancing Sweep
feat.unbalancing-sweep.text: You make a great sweep with your weapon or fists about yourself, knocking creatures off their feet and away from you. Choose up to three enemies within your reach and choose whether to [[action.shove|Shove]] or [[action.trip|Trip]] all three of them. Whichever of the two options you choose, roll a separate [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check against each enemy, performing the same action against each enemy. Each attempt counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made all the attempts.
feat.unbound-leaper.name: Unbound Leaper
feat.unbound-leaper.text:
Your jumping prowess is unmatched. You can [[action.leap|Leap]] up to 30 feet in any direction without touching the ground and without requiring an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check; when doing so, you must land on a space of solid ground within 30 feet of you, or else you fall after using your next action. You can exceed your normal Speed while Leaping.

**Special** If you have the [[feat.fantastic-leaps|Fantastic Leaps]] feat, the total distance you can Leap horizontally is 40 feet, and the total distance you can Leap vertically is 35 feet.
feat.unburdened-iron.name: Unburdened Iron
feat.unburdened-iron.text:
You've learned techniques first devised by your ancestors during their ancient wars, allowing you to comfortably wear massive suits of armor. Ignore the reduction to your Speed from any armor you wear.

In addition, any time you're taking a penalty to your Speed for some other reason (such as from the encumbered condition or from a spell), deduct 5 feet from the penalty. For example, the [[condition.encumbered|encumbered]] condition normally gives a –10-foot penalty to Speed, but this feat would reduce it to a –5-foot penalty. If your Speed is taking multiple penalties, pick only one penalty to reduce.
feat.uncanny-agility.name: Uncanny Agility
feat.uncanny-agility.text: You have near-supernatural poise that lets you move swiftly across the most unsteady surfaces. You gain the [[feat.steady-balance|Steady Balance]] skill feat. You can Step into difficult terrain caused by uneven ground, such as a rocky field, hilly incline, or rocking ship.
feat.uncanny-bombs.name: Uncanny Bombs
feat.uncanny-bombs.text: You lob bombs unerringly, despite obstructions or distance. When you throw an [[trait.alchemical|alchemical]] item with the [[trait.bomb|bomb]] trait, its range increment increases to 60 feet, you reduce any circumstance bonus to the target's AC from cover by 1, and you automatically succeed at the flat check when targeting a [[condition.concealed|concealed]] creature.
feat.uncanny-cheeks.name: Uncanny Cheeks
feat.uncanny-cheeks.text: You gain the [[feat.prescient-consumable|Prescient Consumable]] and [[feat.prescient-planner|Prescient Planner]] feats, except that you always withdraw the objects from your cheek pouches. This means the object you retrieve must fit in your cheek pouches; this is generally an item of negligible Bulk unless you also have the [[feat.cheek-pouches|Cheek Pouches]] feat.
feat.uncanny-dodge.name: Uncanny Dodge
feat.uncanny-dodge.text: You gain the [[class.rogue|deny advantage]] class feature.
feat.unconventional-weaponry.name: Unconventional Weaponry
feat.unconventional-weaponry.text:
You’ve familiarized yourself with a particular weapon, potentially from another ancestry or culture. Choose an uncommon simple or martial weapon with a trait corresponding to an ancestry (such as [[trait.dwarf|dwarf]], [[trait.goblin|goblin]], or [[trait.orc|orc]]) or that is common in another culture. You gain access to that weapon, and for the purpose of proficiency, you treat it as a simple weapon.

If you are trained in all martial weapons, you can instead choose an uncommon advanced weapon that has an ancestry’s trait or is common in another culture. You gain access to that weapon and have familiarity with that weapon. For the purpose of proficiency, you treat it as a martial weapon.
feat.undaunted.name: Undaunted
feat.undaunted.text: Your spirit has endured many challenges over its long existence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against [[trait.emotion|emotion]] effects. If you roll a success on a saving throw against an emotion effect, you get a critical success instead.
feat.undead-slayer.name: Undead Slayer
feat.undead-slayer.text: Your knowledge of your own not-quite-living anatomy, combined with your experience in combat, helps you take down undead foes with ease. Against [[trait.undead|undead]] creatures, you gain a circumstance bonus to damage with weapon and unarmed Strikes equal to the number of weapon damage dice for the Strike. This bonus increases to double the number of weapon damage dice if your target has the [[trait.vampire|vampire]] trait.
feat.underground-network.name: Underground Network
feat.underground-network.text:
You're connected to groups that know what's going on in the streets, and you can get information out of them quickly. When you use Society to [[action.gather-information|Gather Information]] in an area where you have a network (typically a settlement where you've spent at least a week or spent a day of downtime to build a network faster), you can contact a member of these groups to get information directly from them. This usually takes about an hour, and it doesn't draw as much attention as Gathering Information in public might. The check and information gained otherwise follow the normal rules for Gather Information. 
In addition, if you have successfully consulted the underground network, you get a +1 circumstance bonus to the next check to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] you attempt about the subject you were Gathering Information on, or a +2 circumstance bonus if you're using Underworld Lore for the check. The GM might change the Lore skill related to the network depending on your location or the specifics of the network you're tapping into.
feat.underhanded-assault.name: Underhanded Assault
feat.underhanded-assault.text: You capitalize on the distraction provided by an ally. You Sneak up to a foe adjacent to one of your allies. You can roll against the foe you’re Sneaking up on, even if it’s currently observing you, as though you were hidden. You take a –2 penalty on your Stealth check. If your Stealth check against the chosen foe succeeds, you can make a melee Strike against that foe at the end of your Sneak.
feat.underwater-marauder.name: Underwater Marauder
feat.underwater-marauder.text: You’ve learned to fight underwater. You are not off-guard while in water, and you don’t take the usual penalties for using a bludgeoning or slashing melee weapon in water.
feat.underworld-investigator.name: Underworld Investigator
feat.underworld-investigator.text: Your work as an investigator makes you familiar with the criminal element. You might be a criminal yourself, or you might have gained an understanding of how they operate from the outside. You become trained in [[skill.lore|Underworld Lore]], and you gain your Pursue a Lead investigation bonus to [[skill.thievery|Thievery]] checks to investigate a case (such as checks to [[action.steal|Steal]] a clue from a suspect or [[action.pick-a-lock|Pick a Lock]] to open a safe with damning documents).
feat.undying-ferocity.name: Undying Ferocity
feat.undying-ferocity.text: You resist death’s clutches with supernatural vigor, daring death to claim you while promising that any such attempt will surely fail. When you use [[feat.orc-ferocity|Orc Ferocity]], you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level.
feat.unfettered-halfling.name: Unfettered Halfling
feat.unfettered-halfling.text: You were either pressed into indentured servitude or shackled in a prison, but you've since escaped and have trained to ensure you'll never be caught again. Whenever you roll a success on a check to [[action.escape|Escape]] or a saving throw against an effect that would impose the [[condition.grabbed|grabbed]], [[condition.immobilized|immobilized]], or [[condition.restrained|restrained]] condition on you, you get a critical success instead. Whenever a creature rolls a failure on a check to [[action.grapple|Grapple]] you, it gets a critical failure instead.
feat.unhampered-passage.name: Unhampered Passage
feat.unhampered-passage.text: You won't allow others to restrain you. You can cast [[spell.unfettered-movement|_unfettered movement_]] on yourself as a primal innate spell once per day.
feat.unified-theory.name: Unified Theory
feat.unified-theory.text: You understand the common underpinnings of the four traditions of magic and magical essences, allowing you to understand them all through an arcane lens. Whenever you use a skill action or a skill feat that requires a Nature, Occultism, or Religion check, depending on the magic tradition, you can use Arcana instead. If you would normally take a penalty or have a higher DC for using Arcana on other magic (such as when using Identify Magic), you no longer do so.
feat.unimpeded-step.name: Unimpeded Step
feat.unimpeded-step.text: With a burst of divine liberation, your ally's movement from your [[action.liberating-step|Liberating Step]] is unaffected by difficult terrain, greater difficult terrain, narrow surfaces, and uneven ground. If you have the exalted reaction benefit, this applies to everyone who Steps.
feat.universal-longevity.name: Universal Longevity
feat.universal-longevity.text: You’ve perfected your ability to keep up with all the skills you’ve learned over your long life, so you’re almost never truly untrained at a skill. You reflect on your life experiences, changing the skill you selected with [[feat.ancestral-longevity|Ancestral Longevity]] (and the skill you selected with [[feat.expert-longevity|Expert Longevity]] if you have that feat).
feat.unmistakable-lore.name: Unmistakable Lore
feat.unmistakable-lore.text: You never get information about your areas of expertise wrong. When you Recall Knowledge using any Lore subcategory in which you’re trained, if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. If you’re a master in a Lore subcategory, on a critical success, you gain even more information or context than usual.
feat.unobstructed-shot.name: Unobstructed Shot
feat.unobstructed-shot.text: With a quick use of brute force, you remove an obstacle and take a calculated shot as part of the same motion. Attempt to [[action.shove|Shove]] or [[action.trip|Trip]] one adjacent creature, then make a ranged Strike with a bow or crossbow you're wielding. The Strike is made at the same multiple attack penalty as the Shove or Trip attempt, and this activity counts as one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty.
feat.unseat.name: Unseat
feat.unseat.requirements: You are riding your mount and wielding a [[trait.jousting|Jousting]] weapon.
feat.unseat.text: With a mighty blow from atop your companion, you attempt to knock an opponent off their mount. Make a melee [[action.strike|Strike]] against a mounted creature. If your attack hits, attempt an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check against the target’s Fortitude DC. If you succeed, the target is knocked off its mount into a space of its choice adjacent to its mount. If you critically succeed, the target also lands prone.
feat.unstable-concoction.name: Unstable Concoction
feat.unstable-concoction.text: You can mix a wondrous yet volatile liquid into an [[trait.alchemical|alchemical]] [[trait.consumable|consumable]] if it has an initial effect that uses dice. You increase the size of any dice for the item's initial effect by one step. For instance, you could increase damage from a [[item.alchemists-fire-moderate|moderate alchemist's fire]] to 2d10 or healing from a [[item.elixir-of-life-moderate|moderate elixir of life]] to 5d8+12. Because this affects only initial dice, it wouldn't increase unarmed attack damage from a [[item.bestial-mutagen|bestial mutagen]], [[condition.persistent-damage|persistent damage]] from an [[item.acid-flask|acid flask]], and the like. When this item is activated, the creature activating it must succeed at a DC 10 flat check or take acid damage equal to the item's level.
feat.unstoppable-juggernaut.name: Unstoppable Juggernaut
feat.unstoppable-juggernaut.text:
You have become a brutal, unstoppable force of nature, able to shrug off mortal wounds with ease. You gain resistance equal to 3 + your Constitution modifier to all damage, and your resistance from raging increases to 8 + your Constitution modifier.

In addition, if you are reduced to 0 Hit Points while raging, you can end your rage as a reaction to stay at 1 Hit Point. If you do, you become [[condition.wounded|wounded 2]] (or increase your wounded condition by 2 if you are already wounded).
feat.untamed-form.name: Untamed Form
feat.untamed-form.text: You are one with the wild, always changing and adapting to meet any challenge. You gain the [[spell.untamed-form|_untamed form_]] order spell, which lets you transform into a variety of shapes that you can expand with druid feats.
feat.untrained-improvisation.name: Untrained Improvisation
feat.untrained-improvisation.text: You’ve learned how to handle situations when you’re out of your depth. Your proficiency bonus to untrained skill checks is equal to your level –2. This improves to your level –1 at 5th level and your full level at 7th level. This doesn’t allow you to use the skill’s trained actions.
feat.unusual-composition.name: Unusual Composition
feat.unusual-composition.text: You can translate the emotion and power of a composition to other mediums. If your next action is to cast a [[trait.composition|composition]] spell that is [[trait.auditory|auditory]] or [[trait.visual|visual]], you can have it affect creatures who can witness it with any sense, not just those the traits indicate, even including special senses like tremorsense. You can choose to exclude any senses you choose.
feat.unusual-treatment.name: Unusual Treatment
feat.unusual-treatment.text:
Your medical training extends to less obvious conditions. When you succeed against a DC 20 check to Treat Wounds, you can also reduce the value of one clumsy, enfeebled, or stupefied condition on the patient by 1. If you’re able to treat more than one creature at once, choose only one to gain this benefit. A creature can benefit from Unusual Treatment only once per day.

If the condition results from an affliction, the affliction isn’t cured, though the condition is reduced as long as the affliction remains at that stage.

If you are a master in Medicine, add the drained condition to the list of conditions you can remove if you succeed at a DC 30 check. If you are legendary in Medicine, you reduce the chosen condition by 2 instead of by 1.
feat.unwavering-mien.name: Unwavering Mien
feat.unwavering-mien.text:
Your mystic control and meditations allow you to resist external influences upon your consciousness. Whenever you are affected by a mental effect that lasts at least 2 rounds, you can reduce the duration by 1 round.

You still require natural sleep, but you treat your saving throws against effects that would cause you to fall asleep as one degree of success better. This protects only against sleep effects, not against other forms of falling [[condition.unconscious|unconscious]].
feat.uplifting-overture.name: Uplifting Overture
feat.uplifting-overture.text: You learn the [[spell.uplifting-overture|_uplifting overture_]] composition cantrip, which aids your allies’ skills with the inspiring nature of your performance.
feat.uplifting-winds.name: Uplifting Winds
feat.uplifting-winds.text: The winds are eager to keep you aloft. When you are flying and Cast a Spell that has the air or electricity traits, you gain a +10 status bonus to your fly Speed, and you can immediately Fly up to half your Speed.
feat.vampire-lore.name: Vampire Lore
feat.vampire-lore.text:
You were raised by your vampiric parent, or you've invested substantial time and energy researching the secrets of your undead progenitors. You're trained in [[skill.religion|Religion]] and [[skill.society|Society]]. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You also gain the [[feat.additional-lore|Additional Lore]] general feat for [[skill.lore|Vampire Lore]].
feat.vandal.name: Vandal
feat.vandal.text:
You have a knack for breaking and dismantling things. Putting them back together is the boring part, so you largely don't bother with that. You become trained in [[skill.thievery|Thievery]]. If you would automatically become trained in Thievery (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

In addition, whenever you hit with a [[action.strike|Strike]] against a trap or an unattended object, you ignore the first 5 points of the object's Hardness.
feat.vengeful-strike.name: Vengeful Strike
feat.vengeful-strike.requirements: You’re under the effect of Come and Get Me.
feat.vengeful-strike.text: When struck by an enemy, you respond in turn. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If the triggering attack was a critical success, you can use Vengeful Strike as a free action instead of a reaction.
feat.vengeful-strike.trigger: A creature within your reach succeeds at an attack against you.
feat.verdant-metamorphosis.name: Verdant Metamorphosis
feat.verdant-metamorphosis.text:
You have turned into a plant version of yourself, gaining the [[trait.plant|plant]] trait and losing traits inappropriate for your new form (typically [[trait.humanoid|humanoid]]). You also gain the Verdant Rest action.

**Verdant Rest** {1a} ([[trait.concentrate|concentrate]]) You turn into a tree or other noncreature plant. This has the effect of using [[spell.one-with-plants|_one with plants_]] to turn into a plant, except that your AC is 30. You can [[action.dismiss|Dismiss]] this effect to turn back. If you rest for 10 minutes in this form in natural sunlight, you recover half your maximum Hit Points. If you take your daily rest in this form, the rest restores you to maximum Hit Points and removes all non-permanent [[condition.drained|drained]], [[condition.enfeebled|enfeebled]], [[condition.clumsy|clumsy]], and [[condition.stupefied|stupefied]] conditions, as well as all poisons and diseases of 19th level or lower.
feat.verdant-weapon.name: Verdant Weapon
feat.verdant-weapon.text:
You cultivate a seed that can sprout into a wooden staff, vine whip, or another weapon. You spend 10 minutes focusing primal energy into a seed, imprinting it with the potential of a single level 0 weapon you are trained with and that has no mechanical parts or metal components. When holding the imprinted seed, you can use an Interact action to cause it to immediately grow into that weapon; a second Interact action returns it to seed form. The verdant weapon can be etched with runes or affixed with talismans as normal, which are suppressed when the weapon is in seed form.

You can have only one verdant seed at a time. If you prepare a second, your first verdant seed immediately becomes a mundane seed; any runes on the previous seed transfer to the new seed at no cost, but inapplicable runes are suppressed.
feat.versatile-font.name: Versatile Font
feat.versatile-font.prereq.1: deity that allows clerics to have both fonts
feat.versatile-font.text: As you explore your deity’s aspects, you move beyond restrictions on healing or harming. You can prepare either harm or heal in the spell slots gained from the harmful font or healing font.
feat.versatile-performance.name: Versatile Performance
feat.versatile-performance.text: You can rely on the grandeur of your performances rather than ordinary social skills. You can use [[skill.performance|Performance]] instead of [[skill.diplomacy|Diplomacy]] to [[action.make-an-impression|Make an Impression]] and instead of [[skill.intimidation|Intimidation]] to [[action.demoralize|Demoralize]]. You can also use an acting Performance instead of [[skill.deception|Deception]] to [[action.impersonate|Impersonate]]. In addition, you can use your proficiency rank in Performance to meet the prerequisites of skill feats that require a particular proficiency rank in Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation.
feat.versatile-signature.name: Versatile Signature
feat.versatile-signature.text: While most bards are known for certain signature performances and spells, you’re always tweaking your available repertoire. When you make your daily preparations, you can change one of your signature spells to a different spell of that rank from your repertoire.
feat.very-sneaky.name: Very Sneaky
feat.very-sneaky.text:
Taller folk rarely pay attention to the shadows at their feet, and you take full advantage of this. You can move 5 feet farther when you take the [[action.sneak|Sneak]] action, up to your Speed.

In addition, as long as you continue to use Sneak actions and succeed at your [[skill.stealth|Stealth]] check, you don't become observed if you don't have cover or greater cover and aren't concealed at the end of the Sneak action, as long as you have cover or greater cover or are concealed at the end of your turn.
feat.very-very-sneaky.name: Very, Very Sneaky
feat.very-very-sneaky.text: You can move up to your Speed when you use the [[action.sneak|Sneak]] action, and you no longer need to have cover or greater cover or be concealed to [[action.hide|Hide]] or Sneak.
feat.vexing-tumble.name: Vexing Tumble
feat.vexing-tumble.text:
You tumble around your foes, expertly avoiding their reactions. Stride up to half your Speed and roll an [[skill.acrobatics|Acrobatics]] check. Compare the result to the Reflex DC of each enemy whose reach you began in or enter during the movement, in sequence.

**Critical Success** This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the enemy, and the enemy is [[condition.off-guard|off-guard]] to you until the end of your turn

**Success** This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the enemy.

**Critical Failure** Your movement immediately stops when you enter the creature's reach; if you began in the creature's reach, you don't move.
feat.vicious-debilitations.name: Vicious Debilitations
feat.vicious-debilitations.text:
The debilitations you dish out seriously impair your foes. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

- **Debilitation** The target gains weakness 5 to your choice of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage.
- **Debilitation** The target becomes clumsy 1.
feat.vicious-evisceration.name: Vicious Evisceration
feat.vicious-evisceration.text: You make a vicious attack that maims your enemy. Make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits and deals damage, the target is [[condition.drained|drained 1]], or drained 2 on a critical success.
feat.vicious-incisors.name: Vicious Incisors
feat.vicious-incisors.text: Your jaws unarmed attack deals 1d6 piercing damage instead of 1d4, and gains the [[trait.backstabber|backstabber]] trait. You can file down your teeth and regrow them later on, enabling you to select this feat at any level, and to retrain into and out of this feat.
feat.vicious-snares.name: Vicious Snares
feat.vicious-snares.text: You deal an additional 1d6 precision damage with damage snares you craft. This increases to 2d6 additional precision damage if you're legendary in Crafting.
feat.vicious-swing.name: Vicious Swing
feat.vicious-swing.text: You unleash a particularly powerful attack that clobbers your foe but leaves you a bit unsteady. Make a melee Strike. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. If you’re at least 10th level, increase this to two extra dice, and if you’re at least 18th level, increase it to three extra dice.
feat.vicious-vengeance.name: Vicious Vengeance
feat.vicious-vengeance.text: While your vengeance is painful for both you and your foe, none can doubt that your enemies suffer more. You gain a circumstance bonus to the damage you deal from [[action.destructive-vengeance|Destructive Vengeance]] equal to the number of damage dice from the reaction. This applies to only the damage the enemy takes, not the damage to yourself or the extra damage you gain after using the reaction.
feat.vigilante-dedication.name: Vigilante Dedication
feat.vigilante-dedication.text:
You have two identities, each with its own name and abilities. Your social identity is an upstanding member of society, while your vigilante identity is a skilled and cunning warrior. Neither of these identities is a false front; you really are both of these people. If someone attempts to discern your other identity, they must use a [[action.seek|Seek]] action to attempt a Perception check against your Deception DC, as if you were using the [[action.impersonate|Impersonate]] action. Your Deception DC against such attempts is 20 + your proficiency modifier instead of the normal DC. Unlike with Impersonate, you don't have to attempt a Deception check to interact with someone to conceal your other identity—a check happens only if someone else specifically tries to uncover your other identity.

Changing from one identity to the other takes 1 minute and must be done out of sight from other creatures. As this process involves both physical changes such as clothing and makeup, along with an altered state of mind, other effects that change your appearance don't reduce the time required to change identities.

Your two identities are completely distinct. Checks to [[action.recall-knowledge|Recall Knowledge]] about one of your identities don't reveal information about the other unless the person attempting the check knows both identities are the same person. Effects that detect you based on your identity work only if you are currently in the identity the effect is trying to detect; otherwise, the effect fails as if the target didn't exist.

To maintain the separation between your identities, some of your abilities have the [[trait.vigilante|vigilante]] trait. Your class feats and vigilante feats are associated with your vigilante identity, and using them while in your social identity may risk exposing you as a vigilante. If your identity is exposed to the public, you lose the benefits of Vigilante Dedication to disguising yourself, but you can spend 1 week of downtime to create a new social identity.
feat.vigorous-anthem.name: Vigorous Anthem
feat.vigorous-anthem.text: You instill magical vigor in your allies when you inspire them to attack. If your next action is to cast the [[spell.courageous-anthem|_courageous anthem_]] [[trait.composition|composition]] cantrip, you and all affected allies gain temporary HP equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier that last for 1 minute.
feat.vigorous-health.name: Vigorous Health
feat.vigorous-health.text: You can withstand blood loss startlingly well. Whenever you would gain the [[condition.drained|drained]] condition, you can attempt a DC 17 flat check. On a success, you don't gain the drained condition.
feat.viking-dedication.name: Viking Dedication
feat.viking-dedication.text:
Vikings spend long periods of time at sea, only to leap from their boats at a moment's notice, charge through the surf, and take their enemies by storm. You gain the [[feat.additional-lore|Additional Lore]] general feat for Sailing Lore and Warfare Lore. 
When using your land Speed, you ignore difficult terrain from shallow water, such as in bogs or on beaches. In addition, if you roll a success on an [[skill.athletics|Athletics]] check to [[action.swim|Swim]], you get a critical success instead.
feat.viking-weapon-familiarity.name: Viking Weapon Familiarity
feat.viking-weapon-familiarity.text:
From childhood, you have been exposed to traditional viking combat techniques, and you soon learned to handle axe, sword, and shield in battle. Now, you can raid proudly alongside your fellows. You gain the [[feat.shield-block|Shield Block]] reaction. Additionally, you have familiarity with the [[item.battle-axe|battle axe]], [[item.hatchet|hatchet]], [[item.longsword|longsword]], [[item.shield-boss|shield boss]], [[item.shield-spikes|shield spikes]], and [[item.shortsword|shortsword]]—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these weapons as simple weapons.

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.
feat.virtuosic-performer.name: Virtuosic Performer
feat.virtuosic-performer.text: You have exceptional talent with one type of performance. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when making a certain type of performance. If you are a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2. Select one of the following specialties and apply the bonus when attempting Performance checks of that type. If it’s unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides.
feat.vivacious-bravado.name: Vivacious Bravado
feat.vivacious-bravado.text: Your ego swells, granting you a temporary reprieve from your pain. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Charisma modifier that last until the start of your next turn.
feat.vivacious-conduit.name: Vivacious Conduit
feat.vivacious-conduit.text: Your connection to the fey world has grown, and its vital energy flows into you rapidly. If you rest for 10 minutes, you regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier × half your level. This is a healing [[trait.vitality|vitality]] effect and is cumulative with any healing you receive from [[action.treat-wounds|Treat Wounds]].
feat.voice-of-the-night.name: Voice of the Night
feat.voice-of-the-night.text: You hear and understand the words of creatures you share the darkness with. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [[skill.diplomacy|Diplomacy]] skill with bats, rats, and wolves. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on such animals.
feat.void-siphon-cleric.name: Void Siphon
feat.void-siphon-cleric.text: The raw energy of the Void saps the essence of the living. Any living creature that critically fails its save against a harm spell you cast is drained 1.
feat.voluminous-vials.name: Voluminous Vials
feat.voluminous-vials.text:
Your number of versatile vials per day increases to 5.
